This brings us to off page SEO, also known as backlinks, since your competition can also have similar website content. How does Google decide who will rank higher? This is where backlinks come into play. A backlink is a clickable link from one website to another, and Google considers this as a vote of confidence. So the more quality backlinks you have, the better your rankings will be. These are some of the free and paid options to build links to your real estate website. Pause the video and have a look. Links that are harder to obtain are usually considered more valuable. For example, anyone can create a post on Medium.com and add a link to their website. That link has almost no value to Google because there are thousands of such links created every day. On the other hand, getting mentioned on a real estate forum is like winning the SEO jackpot. I hope this video points you in the right direction. If you need any more help, check out the links in description below.

metadata.title: Programmatic SEO Tutorial ($1,175 MRR in 72 Days Case Study)
metadata.author: Samik Choudhury
metadata.shortDescription:
Programmatic SEO tutorial explaining template-based content generation for Next.js applications. Real case study analyzing Shipper.no's strategy: creating comparison pages, cancel subscription guides, and internal linking architecture that drove $1,175 MRR in 72 days through organic traffic.

Timestamps:

0:00 - Introduction: Programmatic SEO for Internet Business
0:28 - What is Programmatic SEO Explained
1:17 - Template Creation: JSON vs Markdown vs Array
2:13 - Static Page Generation Benefits
2:38 - Shipper.no Case Study Introduction
3:37 - Blog Strategy: Cancel Subscription Guides
4:17 - Internal Linking Strategy Breakdown
5:12 - Google Crawler Benefits Analysis
6:09 - Template Structure Demonstration
6:57 - Results: David's 72-Day Journey to $1,175 MRR

What is Programmatic SEO:

Create one template (JSON, Markdown, or Array) reusable across multiple pages. Template contains structured data iterated for each blog post. During npm build, static HTML/CSS generated per page. No database calls or API requests needed. Each page gets own optimized HTML for search engines.

Why JSON/Markdown Over Database:

Next.js deployment with JSON/Markdown templates enables static generation without API calls. Build process creates individual HTML files for each blog entry. Faster page loads and better SEO than dynamic database queries. No server-side rendering overhead. Perfect for content-heavy sites prioritizing organic traffic.

Shipper.no Analysis:

Lovable and Bold.new alternative with strategic SEO focus. Footer comparison pages: Shipper vs Cursor, Lovable, Replit, Bold. Blog template: "How to cancel [competitor] subscription" guides. Each post follows identical structure with different competitor data. Simple execution but masterful SEO implementation.

Internal Linking Strategy:

Seven internal links found in single "Cancel Lovable" article. Links include: Lovable pricing, Lovable review, Shipper features, export guides. Google crawler discovers and indexes all linked pages. Improves domain authority and page rank. Human readers explore related content naturally.

Template Structure Components:

Header with consistent branding across all posts. Author name and profile image. Article summary with key points. Left sidebar: clickable table of contents with auto-scroll. Right sidebar: email signup for updates. Main content: step-by-step guide format. Internal links embedded throughout text.

Real Results Case Study:

David (Shipper founder) achieved $1,175 MRR in 72 days post-launch. Strategy: Reddit engagement plus aggressive SEO. Shared playbook publicly on social media. Bullish on organic traffic over paid acquisition. Template approach enabled rapid content scaling without hiring writers.

Implementation Benefits:

Domain ranking boost from multiple indexed pages. Domain authority increase through internal linking. Competitor keyword targeting without direct competition. Discovery traffic from comparison searches. Educational content builds trust before conversion. Scalable content creation requiring minimal resources.

Key SEO Principles:

Breadcrumbs improve navigation and crawler understanding. Internal linking passes page authority throughout site. Template consistency helps search engines understand site structure. Static pages load faster improving user experience. Content targeting competitor keywords captures intent-driven traffic.

Programmatic SEO - if you’re a small business owner trying to grow smarter, pull up a chair: this video gives you a clear, no-jargon way to decide whether it truly fits your products, data, and budget in today’s AI-first search landscape. 

You’ll learn how to recognize the conditions where it actually works, spot the hidden risks (like tech/content debt and AI answers stealing clicks), and follow a simple, test-first path to validate before you scale. 

The result? A confident yes/no decision, fewer wasted pages, and a focused roadmap to build only what attracts qualified traffic and real revenue, so programmatic SEO becomes a growth lever, not an expensive trap.

Using an expired domain is one of the most high leverage ways to rank faster on Google. SEO takes time, and in my recent video I talked about how it can take six to twelve months for a new directory to start showing up on the first page for target keywords. The only real way to speed that up is through backlinks.

The problem is that building backlinks from scratch is expensive and time consuming. That’s why expired domains can be such a huge opportunity. When you buy an expired domain that already has strong backlinks pointing to it, you’re basically starting with built-in authority and giving your site a head start.

In this video, I’ll show you how I find and vet expired domains so you can spot the ones worth investing in.

03:12 Vetting an expired domain (Full backlink analysis)

What happens when someone forgets to renew their domain?

It doesn’t disappear.

In many cases, that domain goes back on the market — still carrying years of SEO history, backlinks, and even Google trust.

In this video, we explain what an expired domain really is, how it works in SEO, and 4 powerful ways expired domains can boost your rankings when used correctly.

If you’ve ever seen a brand-new website rank on page one much faster than expected, chances are they didn’t start from zero — they started with an expired domain.

This guide is designed for SEOs, affiliate marketers, niche site builders, and anyone who wants to rank faster without using risky shortcuts.

📌 What You Will Learn

- What an expired domain is and how it differs from aged domains
- How expired domains retain SEO history and backlinks
- Why expired domains can give you instant SEO momentum
- How backlink inheritance actually works
- When 301 redirects pass authority — and when they don’t
- How to rebuild expired domains safely without triggering penalties
- The biggest risks of expired domains and how to avoid them

🕒 Timestamps

00:00 – What happens when a domain expires
01:13 – What is an expired domain 
02:13 – How expired domains work for SEO
03:23 – SEO momentum and the head start effect
04:13 – Backlinks that still pass authority

05:59 – Rebuilding expired domains as full websites
06:53 – Risks and red flags you must check
07:23 – Final recap: 4 ways expired domains boost SEO
08:00 – Where to find clean expired domains

✅ Key Takeaways

- Expired domains are not “new” domains — they come with history
- Clean backlink profiles can transfer authority to new projects
- Relevance matters more than domain age
- Page-level rebuilding preserves link equity
- Poor domain history can destroy SEO before it starts
- Smart research separates SEO shortcuts from SEO disasters

🔧 Tools Mentioned

- Wayback Machine
- Google Search Console
- Ahrefs
- Majestic
- Moz / Spamzilla

metadata.title: Topical Authority Isn’t Blog Posts - It’s This
metadata.author: Edward Sturm
metadata.shortDescription:
E925: Most people think topical authority comes from publishing endless blog posts.

That idea is wrong - and it’s why so many SEO strategies fail.

I break down what topical authority really is, how Google actually decides who is an expert, and why links, brand mentions, and bottom-of-funnel pages matter far more than informational content.

This episode is built around a real Reddit thread from an SEO agency trying to move beyond “do SEO and hope it works” into a real, strategic model for winning in search.

We go deep into how topical authority is created, how it works for SaaS, ecommerce, and service businesses, and why most people misunderstand it.

What you’ll learn:
- Why publishing lots of blog posts is not required to build topical authority
- How off-site signals like links, brand mentions, and PR shape how Google sees your expertise
- How bottom-of-funnel landing pages quietly build more authority than blogs ever do
- Why Google cares about the language people use when they mention your brand
- How unlinked brand mentions influence topical relevance
- What Forbes did to become able to rank for almost anything
- How HouseFresh recovered from Google’s Helpful Content Update and 4x’d their traffic
- Why good marketing builds SEO, even when you stop thinking about SEO
- How to use linkable assets, tools, and research to earn authority naturally
- How agencies should think about topical authority when working with multi-category clients
- Why generalist brands can still build topical authority - just across multiple topics
- How to systematize topical authority inside a real SEO playbook

What topical authority actually is:

Topical authority is not something you “do” by writing articles.

It’s the result of:
- Ranking for searches in a topic
- Getting clicks for those searches
- Being mentioned by other websites in the language of that topic
- Earning links where surrounding text reinforces what you’re known for

Google doesn’t need a blog to understand what you do. It needs signals from the rest of the web confirming what you’re associated with.

How real businesses build it…

I explain why the strongest topical authority comes from:

- Bottom-of-funnel SEO pages that target buyers, not readers
- Link building that uses the same language your customers search with
- PR, podcasts, and brand mentions that describe you in your niche
- Tools, research, and resources people actually want to share

When people talk about you using the words that match your business, Google connects your brand to those topics. That’s authority.

If you run an SEO agency…

This episode also covers:
- Why “publish more blog posts” is not a strategy
- How to build topical authority for clients without content factories
- How to decide which topics are worth building authority in
- How to align SEO work with actual revenue

Topical authority should always point toward the searches that make money.

Building Topical Authority: How to Gain Traction For a New Topic (James Dooley ft David G Quaid)

https://youtu.be/mE2Y-3fNorE
https://www.youtube.com/@UCHbtzKwhxTCv2b85um7880A 

James Dooley and David G Quaid discuss how to build topical authority when entering a new subject with little existing authority. They cover cornerstone content, keyword difficulty, semantic relevance, long-tail keywords, internal linking and why starting with easier terms can help you gradually compete for more valuable searches.

metadata.title: Mediavine vs. Raptive: Which is Better for Bloggers?
metadata.author: She Knows SEO
metadata.shortDescription:
I compare two popular ad networks for bloggers, Mediavine and Raptive (formerly Adthrive), and which will make you more money. I discuss the differences between them, including requirements, revenue share, and payment periods. 
I also share my personal experience and insights on how these networks have helped me monetize my sites. If you're a blogger looking to optimize your ad revenue, this video will provide valuable information and help you make an informed decision.

Want to get into one of these networks?
Join the Profitable Part-Time Blogger Program! I teach my exact strategies to grow your traffic so you can monetize your blog with these premium ad networks:
https://profitableparttimeblogger.com 

Spreadsheet with Mediavine and Raptive RPM data: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1kNUT9py3BRg4kLnUD20dasCSD0TOZIvZeoMTWsVfE6k/edit?usp=sharing 

Prefer to read it? Check out the case study here: https://sheknowsseo.co/raptive-vs-mediavine/

Join Raptive here: sheknowsseo.co/recommends/raptive

Videos Referenced:
Which Content Optimizer is Best for Bloggers: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=igacyC0EVb4
Raptive Walkthrough: https://youtu.be/xRuzXK8HIFo

metadata.title: How To Increase Your Blog RPM (Mediavine Tips That ACTUALLY Work)
metadata.author: Vitaliy Gershfeld
metadata.shortDescription:
Want to make MORE money from your blog traffic without needing millions of pageviews?

In this video, I break down some of the best ways to increase your RPM and boost your blogging income using strategies that actually work.

If you use Mediavine, Journey, Raptive, Pinterest traffic, SEO, or run a niche/travel blog, these RPM tips can make a huge difference over time.

More case studies: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLTbJJztJG5_QGyPgAXBJHMRDr4SfGkaRC

🔥 In this video:
• What RPM actually means
• Why some blogs earn WAY more than others
• How traffic quality affects RPM
• Best niches for higher ad earnings
• Why session duration matters
• How Pinterest traffic can impact earnings
• Content strategies that improve Mediavine performance
• Simple tweaks that can increase blog revenue

Higher RPM = More income from the SAME traffic.

Whether you're a beginner blogger or already monetized with Mediavine, this video will help you understand how to maximize your earnings potential.

Subscribe for more videos on:
• Blogging
• Affiliate marketing
• Pinterest traffic
• SEO
• Travel blogging
• Online business growth

#Mediavine #BloggingTips #RPM #MakeMoneyBlogging #SEO

It's an illustration of something that is fundamental to SEO as a business model. SEO traffic is Google's traffic, not yours. You don't own it. You don't control it. You can optimize for it sure, earn it, build a business on it, but it remains entirely subject to decisions made by a company whose interests aren't aligned with yours and who has no obligation to maintain your rankings. Now that's always been true, but the risk of that dependency has increased dramatically in recent years and I think it's now higher than it's ever been. The pattern of Google updates tells the story clearly. Panda, Penguin, Medic, the helpful content update, each one reorganized the search landscape in ways that wiped out categories of legitimate sites operating in good faith and each one has been followed by another because Google's commercial interests and the interests of the affiliate content publishers are not the same and have been diverging for years. The affiliate content squeeze is real and it's intentional. Google has been explicitly reducing the visibility of affiliate content in search results for years now. The helpful content update was in significant part a response to what Google identified as low-value affiliate content and the collateral damage caught genuinely high-quality sites in exactly the same net as the thin spam sites it was supposedly targeting. And then there's the AI content problem. In 2026 the volume of AI generated content competing for the same search rankings as your carefully written affiliate blog is genuinely unprecedented. Google's response, increasingly aggressive quality filtering, disproportionately affects legitimate affiliate content sites. The signals used to identify quality become harder to maintain as AI content floods the index and Google struggles to distinguish between the two. The time investment versus return profile has also shifted fundamentally. Building an affiliate SEO site that generates meaningful income requires months or years of content creation before meaningful traffic arrives. That time investment is made against an uncertain return that is entirely dependent on ranking decisions you have no input into, and the risk-adjusted return on that time investment is deteriorated significantly from where it was 5 years ago. Now, I want to be honest here because this is the revenue tactics video and honesty matters. SEO is not completely dead. There are still people making meaningful money from affiliate content sites in 2026, but they've probably had those websites for a very, very long time. And those results won't be replicable for you guys at home, for instance, who might be just getting started. And also keep in mind those people still having success are not necessarily immune to the next update either. If you're sitting on an organic asset right now that's performing well, I'm genuinely happy for you, but I'd also encourage you to think honestly about how secure that asset actually is and what your plan is on the day that Google decides to reorganize again. So, on the other side of the coin, here's why paid traffic is fundamentally different. This is the most important point in the entire video and it comes directly from the Tennis Bros experience. The fundamental problem with SEO and with any organic traffic model is that you don't control the traffic, you influence it. You can get very good at influencing it. You can build genuine expertise in understanding what Google rewards and build content that earns rankings and holds them for years, but you don't control it. And when you don't control your traffic, you don't truly control your business. With paid traffic, this is where you can go to companies like Facebook, Google, native advertising networks, and buy ads directly. The dynamic is completely different. You decide how much to spend, you decide where to spend it, you decide what to send it to and when. The platform cannot remove your ability to buy traffic in the same way Google can remove your organic rankings overnight. The results are determined by your decisions, your offer selection, your creative quality, your landing page structure, your testing discipline, not by an algorithmic update you'll never see coming. Now, that control is the reason I've always been a paid ads guy. Not because SEO doesn't work, the tennis pro has proved it can work extraordinarily well, but because the moment I understood that my organic traffic could be removed by decision I had no input into, I knew that wasn't the foundation I wanted to build my primary income on. The testing and iteration of answer paid traffic is also genuinely significant. A paid traffic affiliate can launch a new offer, gather meaningful data and make optimization decisions within days. An SEO affiliate building content around new offer waits months for Google to index and rank that content, by which time the offer may have peaked, the angle may have been saturated or the competitive landscape may have changed entirely. metadata.title: Google’s November Core Update Is Crushing AI Content Sites
metadata.author: Edward Sturm
metadata.shortDescription:
E1235: Google's November 2026 core update is hitting some websites hard, particularly sites that have scaled AI-generated content. Some SEOs report traffic drops of 75% to 90%, while others are seeing major gains.

I examine traffic data, reports from website owners, whether Google is targeting AI content, and what to do if your rankings have collapsed.

Here's what I cover:

1. Websites losing traffic during Google's November core update
- One website dropped from 200 clicks per day to 20 after its owner rebuilt it with Claude Code and published new content.
- Another site publishing one AI-generated article daily experienced a sharp decline in clicks and impressions.
- Malte Landwehr identified two domains that publicly discussed scaling AI content and subsequently lost rankings.
- One business owner reported a 75% traffic loss despite being one of only two companies making its product.

2. Websites gaining traffic
- One SEO reported growing from 5 monthly clicks to 21,540 in 16 days.
- Another website owner reported a 6X recovery after the December 2025 core update.
- Other site owners report stable rankings or modest increases.
- Why overall industry chatter is quieter than during a typical core update.

3. Is Google targeting AI-generated content?
- Reports of major losses from websites that scaled AI content.
- Google's guidance on manually fact-checking and reviewing AI-generated content.
- Why I believe Google could evaluate AI usage across an entire site.
- Why Google's Deep Review fact-checking tool doesn't explain the changes.
- The difference between AI-polished writing and unreviewed AI-generated articles.

4. Craig Campbell and James Dooley's AI content experiment
- How they published 1,200 AI-generated articles on a website.
- How traffic grew at first, then collapsed about six months later.
- How removing and replacing the content failed to recover the domain.

5. Are social media platforms taking over Google?
- Facebook's estimated organic traffic reaching an all-time high of 8.2 billion monthly visits, according to Semrush.
- How Reddit, YouTube, Instagram, and X are below their previous traffic highs.
- LinkedIn's estimated Google traffic falling from 769 million to 396 million monthly visits.
- How LinkedIn remains useful for parasite SEO.

6. What to do if your website was hit
- Why minor traffic fluctuations are normal, especially for smaller websites.
- How you should wait for the core update to finish rolling out.
- Identify the pages experiencing the biggest declines.
- How to reassess search intent, content quality, and above-the-fold answers.
- What to examine in page titles, URLs, H1s, and internal links.
- Why you should keep publishing bottom-of-funnel landing pages.

Don't confuse normal volatility with a major traffic collapse. If your site has suffered a steep decline, take a critical look at whether your pages deserve to rank. If your rankings are stable, keep building.

metadata.shortDescription:
Today we covered Google November 2026 core update being released. OpenAI released the ChatGPT business hub and we have click data.  Yahoo Scout is out of beta with 3 billion answers and Yahoo announced Pivot Search.  Google lost again to SerpApi. Google Ads new performance max page feeds update. 

0:00 - Introduction
0:52 - Google November 2026 core update
3:31 - ChatGPT Business hub is out, with click data
7:14 - Google loses again to SerpApi over scraping
9:07 - Google Ads PMax page feeds
11:49 - Yahoo Scout is out of beta with Pivot Search
14:45 - Conclusion

A daily recap video summarizing a few of the top search marketing headlines covered at the Search Engine Roundtable.

This recap is called It's New - A quick, daily dose of the latest in SEO with Anu Adegbola of Search Engine Land, Mordy Oberstein of SE Ranking and Greg Finn of Cypress North (and Marketing O’Clock) and Barry Schwartz.

Google has officially released the November 2026 Core Update! 🚨 This update may impact website rankings, organic traffic, and search visibility across different industries.

In this video, we'll discuss the November 2026 Google Core Update, what it means for website owners, and how SEO professionals should prepare.

If you are an SEO professional, blogger, website owner, or digital marketer, this update is important to understand.

Subscribe for more SEO updates, Google algorithm news, and digital marketing tutorials.

Google's November 2026 Core Update is an important opportunity to rethink your SEO strategy.

In this video, I'm explaining how to analyse your website after the November Core Update, compare your webpages with competing websites, identify content gaps, improve webpage quality, and build a stronger SEO strategy based on what users actually need.

This is not just another Google algorithm update discussion. I've covered the practical implementation process, including what you should analyse, what you need to improve, and which SEO practices you should avoid.

WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS VIDEO:

How to analyse your website after the November 2026 Core Update
How to compare your webpages with currently competing pages
How to identify content gaps and missing information
How to improve webpage quality and usefulness
How to analyse competitor content and page structure
What to improve in your existing webpages
How to identify areas where your content needs more depth and clarit
What SEO activities you should avoid
How to build a practical SEO action plan after the update

How to approach long-term rankings instead of chasing temporary SEO tricks

WHO SHOULD WATCH THIS VIDEO?
SEO professionals, digital marketers, website owners, bloggers, SEO agencies, and businesses that want to understand how to improve their websites after Google's November Core Update.

My recommendation: Don't randomly rewrite your pages or make unnecessary website changes just because Google released an update. Analyse your data, compare relevant competitors, understand search intent, identify genuine weaknesses, and make improvements that provide real value to users.

Watch the complete video and follow the practical process explained in the dashboard.

If you work in SEO, save this video and use the process while reviewing your important webpages.

कोई भी चेंज मत करो। आज से 24 नवंबर तक कोई भी बदलाव मत करो। ना टाइटल में छेड़छाड़ करो, ना आप किसी भी आर्टिकल में छेड़छाड़ करो। ठीक है? कोई भी पेजेस में कोई बदलाव मत करो, स्कीमा में कोई बदलाव मत करो। अच्छे से मॉनिटर करना है आप। ठीक है? अगर आप कोई भी बदलाव करोगे, कोई भी चेंजेस कर दोगे बीच में देखो बहुत सारे लोग डर की वजह से चेंजेस करना शुरू कर देते हैं। अगर आप चेंजेस करना शुरू करोगे तो पता ही कैसे चलेगा यार कि किस वजह से डाउन हुआ है पेज? अगर देखो कोर अपडेट के टाइम पे ऊपर नीचे होती है ट्रैफिक। अब इसका ये मतलब नहीं है कि डर के मारे आप चीजों को बदलना शुरू कर दो। पहले हमें नोट करना है कि एक्चुअल में क्या हो रहा है। बहुत लोग जो चेंजेस करते हैं इसी वजह से ही इनका वेबसाइट डाउन हो जाता है। आपका जो वेबसाइट का रैंकिंग है वो वापस आ सकता है। इजीली आ जाता है अपडेट के बाद क्योंकि इस टाइम पे थोड़ा ऊपर नीचे होता रहता है। तो सबसे पहले है फ्रीज हो जाओ। कोई भी बदलाव नहीं करना है आप। फिर सेकंड प्रोसेस शुरू होता है जिसको मैं बोलता हूं कि अपना बेसलाइन नोट करो। ठीक है? एक से 10 नवंबर तक या चलो चलो एक हफ्ते लेके चलते हैं। तीन से 9 नवंबर तक का डेटा नोट करके रख लो। तीन से 9 नवंबर तक आपके पेजेस की क्या पोजीशन थी, कितने क्लिक्स आए थे, कितने इंप्रेशन्स आए थे, आपका एवरेज पोजीशन क्या था, ये आपको नोट करके रख लेना है। जब आप इस चीज को नोट करके रखोगे, इसी चीज को हम यूज करेंगे कंपेयर करने के लिए। और कंपेयर कब करेंगे पता है? जैसे 24 नवंबर को रोल आउट खत्म हो जाएगा। ठीक है? उसके एक हफ्ते बाद हमें और वेट करना है। फिर एक हफ्ते मैं थोड़ा सा और वेट करता हूं। अपने एक्सपीरियंस से आपको बता रहा हूं कि मैं जो भी चेंजेस करूंगा वो कब करूंगा पता है? एक से सात का कंपैरिजन उठाऊंगा और ये जो तीन से नौ नवंबर का कंपैरिजन है उसको उठाऊंगा। देखूंगा कि दोनों में क्या बदलाव हुआ है। तभी तो मुझे पता चल पाएगा ना भाई तीन से नौ नवंबर के बीच में अगर मेरी पोजीशन तीन थी और एक से सात के बीच में अगर मेरी पोजीशन पांच हुई है तो किस वजह से डाउन हुई है ये तो मैं समझूंगा ना। इसके अलावा मैं ये भी देखता हूं कि कौन से पेजेस मेरे डाउन हुए हैं और कौन से पेजेस मेरे अप हुए हैं। तो जो अप हुआ है उसका जो पूरा पैटर्न है उसको मैं समझता हूं कैसे चलो इसको Google ने रिवॉर्ड दिया है, इसको Google ने ऊपर किया है। तो जाहिर सी बात है कुछ तो अच्छा हुआ होगा इस पेज में इसीलिए तो उसको ऊपर किया गया है। तो इन्हीं जो पेजेस हैं जो अप हुए पेजेस हैं उनके पैटर्ns को नोट करता हूं और उनको उठा के जो डाउन हुए हैं उन पेजेस में करता हूं। तो दूसरा आपको प्रोसेस समझ में आ गया ना? पहले तो हमें फ्रीज होना है। दूसरा हमें क्या करना है? तीन से नौ नवंबर का जो डेटा है उसको कलेक्ट करके रखना है। उसका सारा डिटेल कलेक्ट करके रखना है कि भाई कितने क्लिक्स आए, कितने इंप्रेशंस आए और सबसे इंपॉर्टेंट पार्ट है एवरेज पोजीशन मेरा क्या था उस वक्त और अभी एक से सात दिसंबर को जब हम कंपेयर करेंगे तब हम देखेंगे कि क्या बदलाव आया है। ये पूरा पॉइंट्स नोट करके रख लो और सात तारीख को मैं फिर एक नया वीडियो बनाऊंगा जहां पे हम कंपैरिजन करेंगे। अगर मैं भूल भी जाऊं तो मेरे को कमेंट सेक्शन में याद दिला देना डेफिनेटली हम इस पे बात करने वाले हैं। इसके बाद मैं अपने मनी पेजेस की पूरी लिस्ट बनाता हूं। देखो ऑलरेडी हमने तीन से नौ नवंबर का डेटा निकाल लिया है, सारे पेजेस का निकाला है। अब मैं इंपॉर्टेंट पेजेस का भी डेटा निकाल कर रखूंगा। ये जो इंपॉर्टेंट पेजेस का डेटा है उसको हम अच्छी तरीके से समझेंगे। अब ये मेरे इंपॉर्टेंट पेजेस हैं। इसको तो मुझे किसी भी हाल में ऊपर रखना ही है। तभी तो मुझे सेल्स आएगा, तभी तो मुझे लीड्स आएगा। अभी जो मेरे इंपॉर्टेंट पेजेस हैं अगर ये पांच पोजीशन से ज्यादा नीचे गिरते हैं और तीन दिन में रिकवर नहीं होते हैं तब मैं इन पे ज्यादातर काम करना शुरू करूंगा। एक या दो दिन से कुछ नहीं होगा कम से कम तीन दिन वेट करो। तीन दिन में अगर वापस नहीं आता है तब हम इसमें चेंजेस करना शुरू करेंगे, तब हम इसमें बदलाव करना शुरू करेंगे। ये टाइम का प्रोसेस बता रहा हूं जो सात तारीख का प्रोसेस है, सात दिसंबर का प्रोसेस है। इसी एक से सात के बीच में हम चीजों को चेक करेंगे, लेकिन इससे पहले मैं अपने मनी पेजेस का भी लिस्ट बनाते चलूंगा और इन इस पूरे अपडेट के दौरान मैं ये भी देखूंगा कि कौन-कौन से मेरे पेजेस अप हुए और डाउन हुए। यही जो डाउन वाले जो मनी पेजेस अगर वो डाउन होते हैं तो मैं ये नोट करके रखूंगा। ठीक है? अगर ये तीन दिन में वापस नहीं आते अपने एक्चुअल पोजीशन में तब फिर मैं आगे का पूरा प्लान बनाने वाला हूं। यही सेम चीज आपको करना है। तो ये तीन पॉइंट हमारा कंप्लीट हो गया, अच्छे से समझ में आ गया। कोई भी डिफिकल्टी आती है, कमेंट सेक्शन में तुरंत मेरे से पूछना। इसके बाद रोल आउट के कंप्लीट होने का अच्छी तरीके से इंतजार करना। देखो Google बोल सकता है दो हफ्ते तो लगेगा ही है यानी कि 24 नवंबर तक वेट करना है। अब 24 नवंबर के बाद मैं क्या बोला था? एक हफ्ते और रुकेंगे यानी कि हम 1 दिसंबर तक लेके चलते हैं। जो भी चेंजेज हैं, बदलाव है वो हम 1 दिसंबर से शुरू करेंगे। इसीलिए देखो मैं तो हमेशा से बोल रहा हूं कि एक हफ्ते नहीं बल्कि दो हफ्ते रुक लेना। क्या होता है यार अगर आप दो हफ्ते रुकोगे आपको रियल डेटा मिल जाएगा। देखो 24 नवंबर को अपडेट खत्म हो रहा है। इसके बाद एक हफ्ते मैं रुकने बोल रहा हूं यानी कि 1 दिसंबर तक के। 1 दिसंबर के बाद एक हफ्ता और रुक लो ताकि डेटा आ जाए। 1 से 7 दिसंबर का डेटा हमारे पास आ गया है। जो जो कंटेंट में बदलाव करने हैं हमें क्लियर कट पता चल जाएगा क्योंकि ऊपर जाने वाले पेजेस का लिस्ट मिल जाएगा और नीचे जाने वाले पेजेस का लिस्ट मिल जाएगा। नीचे गए तो क्यों गए इसको हमें समझना पड़ेगा क्योंकि कंपैरिजन जब हम करेंगे तीन से नौ का और यहां पे एक से सात का तब हमें क्लियर कट सब समझ में आ जाएगा। तो जो ऊपर जाने वाले पेजेस हैं उसी का पैटर्न हम नए पेजेस में लगा देंगे। और जो सेल्स का यू नो देखो जो अभी ब्लैक फ्राइडे के टाइम पे सेल्स पे काम करने वाले हैं ठीक है जो आपके सेल पेजेस हैं उसको आप एकदम ज्यादा बदलाव मत करना। अभी के टाइम की बता रहा हूं अभी कोई बदलाव मत करना। प्राइसिंग, स्कीमा, टाइटल ये सब कुछ मत बदलो। ठीक है? ये सब हम बाद में करेंगे जब प्रॉपर एक से सात तारीख के बाद हम उस चीज पे काम करेंगे। उसी टाइम पे हम सारी चीजों को अच्छी तरीके से मॉनिटर करेंगे। अगर आपको सेल चलानी है तो कोई बदलाव मत करो। बाकी देखो फ्रीज करना और सारी चीजों को एनालिसिस करने के लिए आप जो है डेटा निकाल लेना और पूरा चीज आपको स्टेप बाय स्टेप समझ में आ जाएगा। ठीक है? उम्मीद करता हूं देखो मैंने बताने की पूरी कोशिश की है। कभी भी डरना नहीं है। अगर आपने गलती ही नहीं की है बिना स्पैम के एसईओ करते आ रहे हो तो काहे को डरना? सीधा सिंपल सी चीज है आपको समझ समझ के काम करना है। एनालिसिस बहुत जरूरी होता है। एक एसईओ हो तो एनालिसिस करना सीखो। कोई भी डिफिकल्टी आती है अगर आपकी वेबसाइट में डिफिकल्टी आ रही है, आप नहीं कर पा रहे हो आप मेरे को बोलो। मैं उस चीज को फिक्स करके दूंगा। ऑलरेडी हमने काफी सारी वेबसाइट्स को रिकवर कराया हुआ है। एक और चीज मैं आपको कहना चाहूंगा अगर आप प्रोफेशनली डिटेल में एसईओ सीखना चाहते हो तो आप upgrade पीएचपी कोडिंग जिस टाइप का भी आपके पास वेबसाइट है वहां जा के प्रैक्टिस कर पाओगे डिटेल में। ठीक है? उम्मीद करता हूं ये वीडियो आपको पसंद आया होगा। ऐसे इंटरेस्टिंग वीडियो के लिए इस चैनल को जरूर सब्सक्राइब करना। थैंक यू सो मच दोस्तों।

metadata.title: Google Core Update Explained (November 2026): What Google Really Rewards and 8 SEO Fixes
metadata.author: True SEO
metadata.shortDescription:
Google's November 2026 core update is rolling out now. In under five minutes, this video explains what actually happens to your website during a Google core update, why rankings and traffic bounce, and eight simple SEO fixes to protect your site before the next algorithm update.

In March 2024, one Google update wiped 837 websites out of 49,345 tracked from search results. Every one showed signs of AI content. Here's how to make sure your website isn't next.

You'll learn:
1. What Google's crawler (Googlebot) checks on a normal day: real content refreshes, new internal links and topical depth
2. What changes during a core update, in Google's own words, and why a ranking drop doesn't always mean you did something wrong
3. Why every update chases trust, from Panda to E-E-A-T (experience, expertise, authoritativeness, trust) to AI Overviews
4. How often Google releases core updates, and why there's no quiet season
5. What Google said versus what it shows: NavBoost click data and site authority from the leaked documents
6. How Google treats low effort AI content, and how to use AI honestly with your own expertise
7. A real client who came through the last core update and kept growing (active users up almost 62%)
8. Eight SEO tweaks before the next update
9. A Google Search Console plan: what to watch in clicks, impressions and the Pages report, short term and long term

The 8 fixes:
1. A real author, with a name and experience
2. Your own photos and results
3. The answer at the top
4. Update the facts, not just the date
5. Merge thin pages into one strong page
6. Subheadings written as customer questions
7. Internal links from your best pages to the pages that make money
8. Fix anything Googlebot can't read

Sources in this video: Ian Nuttall data via Search Engine Journal and Originality.ai (March 2024 update), SE Ranking (top three results moving after the March 2026 update), Google Search Central (how Search works, core updates guidance), Google's statement on 45% less low quality content (April 2024), US v. Google testimony on NavBoost, the 2024 Google Search API leak, Google's search quality rater guidelines (January 2025), Google Search Console Help.

Rather not do it alone? Book a Strategy Call. We check your website live with you, then once the update lands, compare before and after and send you an in depth report at no charge.
Book here: https://trueseo.co.uk/contact/

0:15 What Googlebot does on a normal day
0:44 What happens in a Google core update

metadata.title: Google’s 2026 Core Update: Why “Good Content” Is No Longer Enough
metadata.author: Kevin C. Roy & GreenBananaSEO's AEO / GEO Mastery
metadata.shortDescription:
Google’s 2026 core update is not a penalty. It is a re-ranking of reality, and weak content is getting replaced by content that proves something.

What You’ll Learn:
- Why this update is really about relevance, trust, and real experience
- Why generic content is losing even if it used to rank
- How EEAT moved from “nice to have” to required everywhere
- Why AI Overviews, Discover, and traditional rankings now share the same signals
- The 3-layer framework: Entity Layer, Content Layer, Schema Layer

Why It Matters:
Rankings alone are no longer enough. If your content is not trusted, structured, and verifiable, you may still rank for a moment, but you will lose visibility across search, Discover, and AI-generated answers.

Question for you:
What do you think is the weakest trust signal on most websites right now? Post your answer in the comments area.

Google also may be showing fewer featured snippets, maybe.  Google Maps review guidelines now disallow incentivizing customers to remove or replace negative reviews. metadata.shortDescription:
In this video you'll learn how to get website traffic with AI now that the all new Google Core Update is rolling out.

Want to make money online, start a business, or get more website traffic from Google? Learn how SEO works, how to use AI to create useful content, and how to build a website that helps potential customers find what you sell.

Build or rebuild your website with Buildy and start your free 10-day trial:  
https://www.buildy.ai

Getting your business online is only the beginning. The next challenge is getting found by people who need your products, services, or expertise.

With Google Search evolving, AI Overviews appearing in search results, and tools like ChatGPT and Gemini changing how people discover businesses, understanding search engine optimization matters more than ever.

In this beginner-friendly SEO deep dive, we explain what Google looks for in helpful content, why search rankings change, and how to use AI to turn your knowledge into website pages that answer real customer questions.

You don’t need to become a programmer or an SEO specialist. You need to understand what makes a page useful, what gives people a reason to trust it, and which questions your future customers are asking.

IN THIS VIDEO, YOU’LL LEARN:

• **SEO for beginners:** What search engine optimization means and how it connects your website with people searching for answers.

• **Google updates explained:** The difference between a ranking change and a Google penalty, and why treating them as the same problem can lead to costly mistakes.

• **E-E-A-T made simple:** How Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness apply to a real business website.

• **AI content for SEO:** How to use artificial intelligence for research, organization, and content creation while adding your own knowledge, examples, and experience.

• **Three SEO traps to avoid:** Fake authority, mass-produced filler, and keyword stuffing.

• **Content that attracts potential buyers:** Why service pages, pricing explanations, buying guides, and answers to customer questions can create valuable opportunities to get found.

• **Google Search Console explained:** What this free tool tells you about the searches that show your pages, the clicks you receive, and problems Google has flagged.

• **A simpler way to build with Buildy:** How to switch on SEO & AI Search, improve your page titles and descriptions, and create more useful website content through plain-English conversation.

If you’re researching how to start an online business, grow a small business, attract customers through organic search, or use AI to support your marketing, this video gives you a practical place to start.

The goal is more than a higher number on a traffic chart. It’s helping the right person find your business, understand your offer, trust what you say, and take the next step.

START BUILDING WITH BUILDY

Have a business idea? Need a website? Already have a site that needs a fresh start?

Tell Buildy what you want to create. Build or rebuild your website, switch on SEO & AI Search, and turn your expertise into service pages, helpful articles, and answers your customers are looking for.

Review what Buildy creates, make changes through conversation, and publish when you’re ready.

Start your free 10-day trial:  
https://www.buildy.ai

HELP CHOOSE THE NEXT DEEP DIVE

Comment **AI** if you want a step-by-step video about creating useful AI content for SEO.

Comment **BUYERS** if you want a deeper guide to finding searches people make when they’re ready to buy and deciding which website pages to create first.

Subscribe for practical videos on starting a business, building websites with AI, getting website traffic, and turning your ideas into a business people can find.

#SEOForBeginners #AIForBusiness #StartAnOnlineBusiness

can still be open for business while
fewer customers ever find it. A page
that slips out of sight can take
inquiries, bookings, and sales with it.
Some supposed SEO shortcuts can make
things worse. A ranking drop and a
Google penalty are two different
problems. You don't need to become an
SEO expert. You need to know the
difference before you start changing
your site. I'll show you what Google's
recent guidance makes clear. Three traps
that can break its rules and how to use
AI to build useful content instead.
We'll decode E-E-A-T with a real-world
example, then switch on Billy's SEO
features and build a plan for getting
found. Stay for the final check before
you delete anything. First, the
distinction that could save you a very
expensive mistake. SEO means search
engine optimization, helping people find
your pages in search. A core update
changes the main systems Google uses to
rank those pages. This one applies
globally across languages, and Google
says the rollout may take two weeks.
Think of your favorite restaurants. A
new place opens, an old favorite
improves, you reorder the list. The
restaurant that moves down hasn't
necessarily done anything wrong. A core
update itself is not a penalty. Spam
violations mean breaking Google's rules
against trying to manipulate search
results. That can lower your site's
visibility or leave pages out
altogether. A human reviewer can also
apply a penalty called a manual action.
You can check for those in Google Search
Console. That's Google's free tool for
seeing how your site appears in Google
Search, which searches show your pages,
which bring clicks, and whether Google
has flagged problems. Think of it as
your website's search dashboard. So
don't treat every drop like a ban, and
don't mistake a shortcut for a recovery
plan. The rules that matter are public.
The surprising part is how far back they
go. In 2011, Google launched Panda, an
update aimed at low-quality content.

history, not a prediction for your site.

500 words. Quick, decide before I

struggling sites for proof of a word

asks them today. Another old question

credit card? That brings us to E-E-A-T.
Experience, expertise,
authoritativeness, trustworthiness. Four
ways to think about why someone should
believe a page. Let's use a made-up
mobile bike repair business. Experience.
Have you actually done the work? Show
the broken chain you replaced with
photos and what happened. Expertise. Do
you understand it? Explain how you
diagnosed the problem and when a part

you recognized as a credible source?
Real customer reviews, relevant
qualifications, and genuine mentions
from others can help show that
reputation. Don't invent them.
Trustworthiness. Can someone rely on
you? Accurate advice, clear prices, real
contact details, an honest explanation
of who's behind the business. Google
says trust is most important. E-E-A-T
isn't one ranking score, and there's no
switch that gives you all four. It's a
quality framework. Google systems use a
mix of signals to identify those
qualities. That matters even more for
advice about health, money, or safety.
Google also asks, who made this? How was
it made? And why does it exist? Show the
real author, the work behind the answer,
and the customer's need. Now, keep that
bike page in mind. What happens if you
try to manufacture the appearance of
expertise instead of showing the real
thing? Separate the news from the rules.

profiles untrustworthy. Put your real
knowledge on the page instead. Trap two,

unoriginal pages mainly to manipulate
rankings without helping people. Google
calls this scaled content abuse. The
policy applies however the content was
made. Trap three, keyword stuffing.

over, or dumping town names onto a page

Google released the November 2026 core update on 10 November 2026. It applies globally and to all languages, and the rollout may take up to 2 weeks. In this video I cover what Google released, what Google's own core update guide says to do (and what to leave alone), and four AI agents that handle it for you. metadata.title: What Is GEO? Generative Engine Optimization Explained (2026): 5 Key Principles
metadata.author: Alex Moreau | AI for Ads & SEO-GEO
metadata.shortDescription:
What is GEO? GEO stands for generative engine optimization: getting your brand named and your pages cited in AI answers, from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity to Google's AI Overviews. The term comes from a 2023 study, and on October 13, 2026 Bing added a beta feature to its GEO tooling that lists the AI searches where other sites appear and yours doesn't. This video builds a checklist of the key principles of GEO while an agent works through them.

The key principles of GEO
1. Measure where AI answers name you
2. Answer first, and back it up with numbers
3. Say something only you can say
4. Let the AI search crawlers in
5. Keep pages current, and check every week

Is GEO different from SEO? Google's AI optimization guide says optimizing for generative AI search is still SEO, because its AI features are rooted in its core Search ranking systems. Bing's guidelines use the word GEO and say it does not guarantee grounding or citations in AI answers.

Do AI answers cost you clicks? Google says AI Overviews have over 2.5 billion monthly users. In a 2025 Pew study of Google searches (March 2025 browsing data), people clicked a regular result on 8% of visits with an AI summary and on 15% without one.

Do statistics help you get cited? In the 2023 study's tests, adding quotes and statistics made pages up to 40% more visible in AI answers: "up to", in the researchers' tests with 2023 models, and visibility inside the answers rather than traffic. Keyword stuffing gave little to no improvement.

Do you need an llms.txt file for GEO? Google's guide says llms.txt will neither harm nor help your visibility in Google Search, because Google Search ignores it. Chrome's Lighthouse checks for it to help AI agents find their way around a site and calls it optional for now, so it's fine to add one.

Which AI crawlers should you let in? OpenAI recommends allowing OAI-SearchBot so your site can appear in ChatGPT search, and Perplexity recommends allowing PerplexityBot. OpenAI's training bot, GPTBot, is a separate switch.

In the demo, the agent shows where a candle store stands in AI answers and who gets named instead. In chat, it works out why a page that ranks on Google gets almost no AI visits and drafts a fix that waits at Approve or Deny (that chat is set to ask; by default it makes changes on its own). It files an Inbox card for a question AI assistants keep answering without naming the store, flags an AI crawler blocked in robots.txt in its weekly audit, and reports each week which assistants sent visitors.

The platform in this video is Ryze. Its AI Visibility asks your tracked questions on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Perplexity, not Google's AI Overviews or AI Mode (Google's Search Console report covers those, with impressions). at HRF studied 75,000 brands and 25 million AI overviews and found five key factors that give
you the best chance of ranking in AI search with GEO. And it all starts with branded mentions.
Large language models like chatbt and Google learn by reading the web. And every time your brand name
appears on a credible site, that becomes another training example. And the more often an LLM sees
your brand connected to a specific topic, the more confidently it associates your name with
that subject when generating answers. It's like when you hear Red Bull, you think extreme sports.
Or when you hear Tesla, you think electric cars. Or when you think of Ahrefs, you think of Sam O,
the charismatic SEO beast. Branded mentions are so important that they have the strongest correlation
with visibility in Google's AI overviews. higher than back links, referring domains, and domain
rating. But how do we know which pages or sites to get mentioned on? According to our research,
get mentioned on highly linked to pages if you want to rank in Google AI overviews and high
traffic pages if you want more visibility in chat GPT and perplexity. To find pages and websites
worth getting mentioned on, go to HF's brand radar and enter your brand, competitors, brands,
niche, and run the search. Then hit the cited domains report where you'll see the top websites,
the number of AI responses, and the exact number of times each brand is getting mentioned and how
they're being mentioned. From here, you can join the Reddit threads AI is pulling from. Reach
out to YouTubers for future reviews or contact publishers for potential PR campaigns. Basically,
you want your brand to appear literally everywhere online, ideally in a positive and topically
relevant way. And that's because of the second key factor for ranking an AI search. Longtail queries.
In traditional SEO, targeting longtail keywords was mostly about coverage. The more queries you
rank for, the more ways there are for searchers to find you. But in AI search, longtail queries
play a different role. AI assistants like Chat GPT may actually use them to decide who to recommend.
And it's because of how AI assistants work. When someone enters a prompt like,
"Plan me a 5-day trip to Japan in November," the AI assistant fans it out into dozens of smaller
longtail subqueries. They then pull information from multiple sources across the web and combine
it into one complete answer. So, if your content ranks for those niche specific queries, your brand
has a much better chance of being included in the AI's final response. And our data backs that up,
showing that Google's AI overviews are way more likely to appear on longer niche queries. So from
a practical standpoint, you should a create content that answers more complex specific
questions and b content clusters that deeply cover the full depth of a topic. But here's the twist.
Even if you've nailed all of this, it might not matter. Because if your content isn't structured
the way AI assistants process information, you may not get as many AI search mentions as you should
be getting. One way Google AI reads content is by using a tree walking algorithm, meaning
it follows the exact semantic HTML structure of a web page from top to bottom. And this makes well-
formatted and structured content easier for it to process. But it's not just about using heading
tags and bulleted lists. It's about how your information flows. Your content should be clear,
organized, and easy to follow. And this matters because when Google or Chat GPT read your page,
they don't process it all at once. They chunk your content into smaller pieces, almost like
reading it paragraph by paragraph, and then they decide which parts are most useful to keep. So,
if your juiciest points are buried deep down or mixed into long, messy sections,
it makes it less efficient for AI to process your content, which may have a role in rankings. Now,
that doesn't mean you should start writing in short, choppy blurbs like an FAQ or make
every paragraph its own idea. Instead, focus on grouping related thoughts together and keeping
each section focused on a single takeaway. Think of it like giving AI a clear outline
where each part should make sense on its own but still naturally connect to the next. Now,
even if your content is perfectly written and structured, there's another key factor that
can put you in or completely knock you out of AI results. And our data shows that this key factor
is all about freshness. Our study of 17 million citations across seven AI search platforms found
that AI assistants strongly prefer newer information. In fact, content cited by AI
is 25.7% fresher than the content that shows up in regular Google results. And Chat GPT and
Perplexity go even further. They tend to list citations from newest to oldest. That happens
because most assistants use something called rag. RAG stands for retrieval, augment, and generation,
which is the part of an AI system that goes out and looks things up. If a model already knows the
answer from its training data, it doesn't need to search again. Just like you and I don't need
to search for directions to places we visit all the time. But if the topic is new or evolving,
Rag steps in and fetches the latest information from the web to fill in the gaps. That's why
freshness isn't just a ranking signal anymore. It's a retrieval signal in this AI era. And here's
proof that freshness can boost your AI rankings. In April this year, HubSpot updated their small
business ideas article and soon saw a massive spike to their organic traffic. No surprises
there, but their AI mentions to that page also spiked at the exact same time, generating over,00
new mentions according to HR brand radar. So something you can do is to take note of pages
that could benefit from regular updates and add them to your regular refresh cycle. Update facts,
new quotes or stats, remove things that have become irrelevant, and redate the post when
it's meaningful. And that one small update could be the difference in getting mentioned across
AI platforms. By the way, I probably should have mentioned this earlier, but before you
do anything, make sure your site can actually be crawled by AI bots. Kind of sounds silly, but in
our study of 140 million websites, about 5.9% were blocking OpenAI's GPT bot alone. So, take
two seconds to go to yourdommain.com/roots.txt and make sure you're not accidentally blocking
the very systems you're trying to rank in. And that brings us to our final, easiest,
and perhaps most important key factor, and it's all about diversifying your strategies. Normally,
when I talk about diversifying your traffic or marketing strategy, it's because over reliance
on a single channel can wipe a business out overnight, which we've seen happen time and
time again. But that's not the reason you should diversify in the context of AI. In our data set,
we compared the top 50 most mentioned domains in Google AI overviews, chat GBT, and Perplexity. And
get this, only seven of those domains appeared on all three lists. That means that 86% of
sources are unique to each assistant. Google AI overviews leans heavily on YouTube, Reddit,
and Quora. Chat GPT prefers publishers and news outlets like Reuters and the Associated Press. And
Perplexity tends to site niche or regional sites like health, finance, and localized blogs. So,
even if you dominate one of these ecosystems, that doesn't mean that you're guaranteed to appear in
the others. Hence, diversification is a must. To find the pages you need to optimize for each AI
platform, go to HF's brand radar and add your brand, a few of your competitors, a niche, and
run the search. Hover over your brand under the AI platform you want to investigate, and hit others
only. Finally, go to the cited pages report to see all of the web pages that are being recommended in
your AI platform of choice where your competitors are mentioned, but you're not. Then, go and reach
out to these websites to try and get your brand mentioned alongside your competitors. And when
you're done with that AI platform, hit the drop down, choose the next AI platform you want to be
mentioned on, and rinse and repeat. Now, a lot of this advice might sound familiar because doing GEO
or AEO or LMO is still just SEO. The difference is that you got to think broader. It's not just
about content and links anymore. It's about building a brand and showing up everywhere
your audience already is. But here's the truth. No one's really saying out loud. No one actually
knows how to definitively optimize for AI search yet. It's still too early. For now, all we have
is the data we've analyzed. And now we need more practitioners to go out there, test, and share the
results. And one of those practitioners is already testing so we can build that step-by-step playbook
for you to follow. So, make sure to subscribe for updates, and I'll see you in the next video.

segments.text: Ask an AI which coffee subscription is
best for espresso. You get a short,
confident answer with two brand names in
it.
[music] If you run one of the other
coffee brands, you're not on page two.
You're simply not there. [music]
That gap between being findable and
being named is what this video is about.
It's called GEO, generative engine
optimization.
[music] In the next few minutes, we'll
cover what changed, what GEO actually
is, how AI answers get built, what the
[music] research says works, and how to
measure it honestly. That last part is
harder than it looks.
[music] Part one, what changed?
For 20 years, search meant a list of
links. [music] You typed a few words,
scanned 10 blue results, and clicked.
Now, a growing share of people [music]
ask an assistant instead. In February
2026, OpenAI said ChatGPT had passed 900
million weekly users.
And search itself changed. In July 2025,
Google said AI overviews, the summaries
at the top of the results, reached more
than two billion people a month. [music]
When an AI summary appears, people click
less. Pew Research tracked real browsing
in the US and found people clicked a
result about 8% of the time with a
summary [music] and 15% without one.
Semrush, using similar web data,
estimated that 68% of US Google searches
in early 2026 ended without a single
click. [music]
None of this means websites stopped
mattering. It means the answer often
happens before the click, and whoever
the answer names gets the attention.
[music] Part two, what GEO is.
The term comes from a research paper by
a team from Princeton and IIT Delhi,
first published in 2023 and presented at
KDD conference in 2024.
[music]
They described generative engines as
systems that search for information and
then write an answer from what they
find. GEO is the work of making your
content more likely to show up and be
cited inside those answers. [music]
Think of it this way. SEO is about where
you rank in a list. [music] GEO is about
whether you're mentioned in a paragraph.
In a list, result number five still gets
seen. In an answer that names two
brands, [music]
number three doesn't exist.
And GEO doesn't replace SEO. Many AI
answers start with a web search, so the
pages that search finds still matter.
[music]
Good SEO is the floor. GEO is what you
build on top of it.
[music] Part three, how an AI answer
gets built.
Roughly, an assistant can answer from
two places. The first is what the model
learned in training. It's memory of the
web frozen at some point in time.
[music] The second is a live search. The
assistant turns your question into one
or more queries, pulls a handful of
pages, [music] reads them, and writes
the answer. Often it cites some of those
pages as sources. [music]
This matters for strategy. Memory
changes slowly and you can't edit it.
Live search you can influence by being
on the pages it finds and by being easy
to read and quote. [music]
Notice too that the pages it finds are
often not yours. Reviews, comparisons,
forums, directories, [music]
the news. If other people describe you
clearly, the answer can repeat it.
[music] And every engine does this
differently. Chat GPT, Gemini, [music]
Perplexity, Claude. Different models,
different search sources, different
habits. [music] Being named in one tells
you little about the others.
Part four, what the research says works.
[music]
In that paper, the team tested nine ways
to rewrite web content on a benchmark of
10,000 queries. [music] the best methods
raised a source's visibility in the
generated answers by up to 40%.
[music] What worked best was
surprisingly plain, citing sources,
adding quotations from credible people,
and adding statistics.
[music] What didn't work was the old
trick of keyword stuffing. Repeating the
target phrase performed worse than doing
nothing at all.
A fair warning, though. That was a
controlled study, and the engines have
changed a lot since. [music] Treated as
a direction, not a guarantee. Anyone
promising guaranteed AI rankings is
guessing.
[music] Part five, a practical playbook.
Step one, make sure AI crawlers can
actually read your site. Check your
robots.txt [music]
for agents like GPT Bot, OAI Search Bot,
Perplexity Bot, and Google Extended.
[music] One blocked line can quietly
keep you out.
Step two, write down the questions your
customers really ask. Not [music]
keywords, questions. Which Espresso
subscription is best? [music] Is it
worth the price? How does it compare to
the other one?
Step three, answer each one plainly near
the top of a page. Specifics beat
slogans, prices, sizes, delivery times,
who it's for, and who it isn't for.
[music] Step four, back it up. Facts
with sources, a real quote, a clear
number. That's exactly the kind of
content the research found engines pick
up. [music]
Step five, show up elsewhere. Get into
honest comparisons, [music] earn
reviews, take part in communities, talk
to the press. Answers often repeat what
others say about you.
[music] Step six, keep pages simple for
machines. Put the important text in the
page itself, not inside images.
Structured data can help a machine
understand a page, but it isn't magic.
And be skeptical of shortcuts. Take
LLMs.txt,
a file meant to guide AI models. Ahrefs
looked at about 137,000
sites. Of the sites that had the file,
97 % got no requests for it at all in a
month. [music]
Part six, measuring it honestly.
Here's the hard part. [music] Ask an AI
the same question twice and you'll often
get a different answer. [music]
SparkToro and Gumroad had hundreds of
volunteers ask 12 questions and
collected almost 3,000 answers from
ChatGPT, Claude, and Google's AI. The
chance that two answers listed the same
brands was less than one in a hundred.
[music]
So a single screenshot proves very
little. It shows one roll of the dice.
Your client sees a different roll
tomorrow and you're both right. [music]
The way out is to measure a rate, not a
moment. Pick a fixed set of questions,
ask each one in each engine, then count
[music]
in how many answers was the brand named.
Say the brand shows up in four answers
out of 12. [music] That's 33 %, but with
only 12 answers, the real number could
be anywhere from about 14 to 60 %. That
range is the margin of error and it
matters. [music]
So if the number moves from 33 to 40,
don't celebrate yet. A real change has
to be bigger than the noise. More
questions and more answers make that
range narrower. [music]
And compare like with like. Same
questions, same engine, same market. A
ChatGPT number next to a Gemini number
isn't a trend. It's two different
measurements.
Beyond whether you're named, look at who
gets named instead, which sites get
cited as sources, and what the AI says
about you. That's where the to-do list
comes from. [music]
Part seven, a simple monthly routine.
Put together, the routine is simple.
Pick 20 to 30 real customer questions,
measure a baseline in each engine you
care about, fix the biggest gaps first,
measure again next month with the same
questions, and report the result
honestly, margin of error included.
[music] That's g e o without the hype.
Be readable, be specific, be talked
about, and measure carefully. [music]
One last thing. If you'd rather not run
all of this by hand, that's why we built
Gen Sig. [music]
You type a website, Gen Sig writes the
questions customers ask in the market
you choose, and you review them before
anything runs. [music]
It asks the a i engines you pick, and
each engine gets its own report.
You see how often the brand is named
with its margin of error, who gets named
instead, the sources cited, and what to
do next. [music]
It won't make an a i recommend you.
Nothing honest can promise that. It
tells you with numbers whether it does.
[music] Thanks for watching. You'll find
Gen Sig at gensig.app.
>> [music]

metadata.title: Topical Authority with 1 Page Exact Match Domain: 8,000 Clicks a Day - Learn Visual Semantics
metadata.author: Koray Tuğberk GÜBÜR
metadata.shortDescription:
Topical Authority is the degree to which a webpage or website is recognized by search engines as a comprehensive, in-depth, and authoritative source on a specific topic or cluster of related subjects, determined through semantic analysis of content depth, relevance, and supporting signals. Visual Semantics describes Google’s process of evaluating a page’s visual layout — including the spatial arrangement of text blocks, images, headings, whitespace, and interactive elements — to infer meaning, relevance, and user experience quality as part of its ranking algorithms.
In this detailed case study, a single-page domain achieved more than 800,000 organic clicks by deliberately building Topical Authority within a compact, one-page structure and leveraging Visual Semantics — all without traditional link building or multi-page content architectures.
Key Topics and Methodologies Covered:

Constructing Topical Authority on a Single Page: How a unified page was engineered with comprehensive topic coverage, semantic internal linking, and entity relationships to establish strong authority signals typically associated with larger content hubs.
Visual Semantics in Practice: An examination of Google’s interpretation of page layout, content hierarchy, and design elements, and how these visual factors directly influence semantic understanding and rankings.
Google’s Query Augmentation: The mechanisms by which Google expands and refines user queries using semantic relationships, and how the page was optimized to align with these expanded interpretations for significantly broader traffic capture.
Multilingual Content Implementation: Specific strategies for delivering multiple language versions on the same one-page domain and the documented effects on global search performance and rankings.
Insights from Google Patents: Analysis of the latest patents concerning visual layout signals, page structure, and their role in modern ranking systems.

The case study reports a verified from 0 to 800,000  increase in organic clicks across a three-month period, with complete methodology, metrics, and implementation steps included.

07:11 – Algorithmic sentence structure and visual page classification
07:50 – Three-month and six-month organic growth results
08:37 – Click satisfaction, conversions, and domain rankability
09:09 – The upcoming SEO Mastermind and Visual Semantics course

metadata.shortDescription:
What is Topical Authority?

A individual or organization's competence or understanding on a certain topic or issue is referred to as topical authority. It gauges a person's or an organization's level of trustworthiness and credibility within a specific sector or industry. Topical authority in the context of search engines can play a significant role in affecting how highly a website appears in search results for a specific topic. For instance, a website that is regarded as the foremost authority on a given subject may appear higher in search results for that subject than a website that is less knowledgeable about the subject.

Why is topical authority important?

Topical authority is significant since it contributes to the development of credibility and dependability. People are more likely to trust and rely on sources that are regarded as authoritative on a given topic when they are looking for information about it. Therefore, having topical authority can aid in boosting website traffic, positioning a business as a thought leader in its sector, and luring potential clients or customers.

Topical authority is crucial in the context of search engines since it can raise a website's placement in search results for a specific topic. This is so because algorithms are used by search engines to evaluate the quality and relevancy of a website's content in light of a particular search query. Due to its reputation as a dependable and trustworthy source of information on the subject, a website that is regarded as the leading authority on a given subject is more likely to appear higher in search results for that subject.

In general, topical authority is crucial because it contributes to the development of credibility, reliability, and knowledge, all of which can be advantageous for both people and organizations.

The suggested videos to understand Topical Authority SEO Case Study with expansion of Topical Maps are listed below.

What is a topical map?

A topical map is a sort of map that displays details regarding a specific subject or topic. This can comprise both concrete elements like mountains, rivers, and cities as well as intangible ideas like geographic boundaries, population density, or economic statistics. Topical maps are used to convey information about a particular topic and can serve a number of objectives, such as those related to education, science, or politics.

A topical map is, in general, a visual representation of data on a certain topic or issue. It can be helpful for a variety of reasons and is used to convey and visualize data.

Topical Maps involve Brand Identity, Source Context, Contextual Bridges for expanding the context, and overall topical graph of the website for better relevance, and expertise signals. Brand and Source Context concepts are processed in the Topical Authority Case Study of @TopicalAuthority.

metadata.title: Topical Authority and Semantic SEO for Local Rankings (Law and Beyond)
metadata.author: Koray Tuğberk GÜBÜR
metadata.shortDescription:
How do historical data, click behavior, visual semantics, topical authority, and page design influence search rankings?

In this technical SEO discussion, Koray Tuğberk GÜBÜR explains how search engines evaluate websites beyond backlinks and written content. The conversation covers document statistics, query statistics, visual page components, local SEO architecture, retrieval cost, and visibility in AI Overviews.

Topics Covered

• Historical data, click behavior, and search engine trust
• Document statistics and query statistics
• Visual semantics and component-based page understanding
• Centerpiece annotation and above-the-fold relevance
• Topical maps for law firms and local businesses
• Core sections versus supporting out-sections
• Service-page architecture and conversion components
• Preventing duplication across location pages
• Cost of retrieval and predictive information retrieval
• Passage ranking, Featured Snippets, and AI Overviews

Concepts

Search engines can evaluate long-term click behavior, branded search demand, user interaction patterns, citations, page structure, and historical document performance.

Pages are not understood only as sequences of sentences. Search engines can process HTML elements, visual blocks, layout hierarchy, interactive features, and the relationships between different components.

The centerpiece annotation represents the main section that communicates the page’s dominant purpose. For a service page, this can include a clear service definition, attorney information, trust signals, supporting visuals, and a visible conversion element above the fold.

For local SEO, the topical map can be divided into two layers:

Core Section: Location-specific commercial pages, such as personal injury lawyer or car accident lawyer pages for individual cities.

Outer-Section:  Supporting topics such as injury types, liability, legal procedures, evidence, medical documentation, insurance claims, and compensation.

Supporting content should strengthen and internally link toward the core commercial pages.

Multi-location pages should include genuinely local information rather than changing only the city name. Relevant courts, hospitals, roads, accident patterns, regulations, neighborhoods, statistics, and local examples can make each page more useful and distinctive.

AI Overview visibility usually begins with strong traditional document and passage ranking. The objective is to create content that search engines can confidently understand, rank, extract, and cite.

Subscribe for more discussions about Semantic SEO, Topical Authority, visual semantics, information retrieval, search engine patents, and website architecture.

In this engaging 5-minute video, Koray Tuğberk GÜBÜR delves into the intricate process of creating effective topical maps tailored for online casinos. Starting with the basics, Koray explains the fundamental concepts and elements needed to construct a topical map, including the categorization of online casinos and various casino games like slots, poker, and the associated features such as payment options and bonuses. The discussion progresses to the importance of source context in shaping the structure of topical maps, highlighting different strategies based on whether the source is a casino affiliate, a direct casino, or a technology provider. Finally, Koray integrates SEO, branding, and technical considerations into the conversation, emphasizing how holistic SEO practices, micro-optimizations, and maintaining relevant content across linked pages can enhance topical relevance and overall site performance. This video is a must-watch for professionals in the casino industry looking to improve their SEO and content strategy.

metadata.author: Koray Tuğberk GÜBÜR
metadata.shortDescription:
Join us in this insightful episode of the Marketing Quacks Podcast as we dive deep into the world of SEO with Koray Tuğberk, a renowned thought leader and the CEO and founder of Holistic SEO. In this episode, hosted by Ryan Dozer, we explore the intricate concepts of holistic and semantic SEO, and how they transform the landscape of search optimization.

Koray shares his journey from managing PBNs to developing groundbreaking SEO strategies that emphasize topical authority and semantic principles. He critically analyzes the current state of SEO, discussing the dominance of major platforms and the evolution of Google’s algorithms over the years. The discussion also covers the balance between optimizing for AI-driven and traditional search engines, the role of AI tools in SEO, and the hype surrounding new technologies in the industry.

Whether you're a seasoned SEO professional or just starting out, this episode offers valuable insights into making your content stand out in an ever-competitive digital world. Tune in to learn how to effectively integrate advanced SEO strategies into your workflow and how to future-proof your content against the constantly changing algorithms.

Watch now to enhance your understanding of holistic SEO and learn from one of the industry's best!

metadata.title: How to Get Cited by AI: External Topical Maps Explained
metadata.author: Koray Tuğberk GÜBÜR
metadata.shortDescription:
External topical maps help search engines understand your authority. Learn how third-party references improve your AI visibility.

We discuss the mechanics of creating a semantics content network across external sources. This approach moves beyond traditional link building, focusing instead on how third-party platforms can be used to signal relevance and authority to AI models and search algorithms.

By strategically placing references in external environments, you provide the context needed for better AI visibility. We break down why this specific SEO strategy is effective for modern search engines that prioritize consensus and entity-based information retrieval over simple keyword matching.

Subscribe for weekly technical SEO breakdowns, and comment which case study topic you want to see analyzed next.

0:00 Intro — External Topical Maps & AI Visibility
0:13 What Is an External Topical Map?
1:13 How the Network Works: Domains, Entity Attributes & the Local Case Study
2:19 Link, Mention, Claim — and Finding Attributes in Google AI Mode
3:13 Filtering Domains, Anchors, Briefs & Publishing Order
3:42 "Wasteful Domains" — Why the Name Should Change
4:11 Query Fan-Out vs Query Augmentation
4:50 Fat Rank vs Checker Trade: First-Party vs Third-Party Claims
6:03 Proof, Claim, Frame & Corroboration Pages
6:55 Why Repetition Creates Consensus
7:10 The 2009 Paper: Answer Scoring & the Truth Range
8:40 Chain of Reasoning, AI Agents & Reverse-Engineering AI Comparisons
9:45 The Single-Page Brand Experiment
10:43 Extension Domains vs External Topical Maps — The Four Layers
11:46 Award Citations & the "Best Lead Generation Agency" Case
12:49 Regulated Niches: Health, Hair Transplants & Fake Statistics
13:43 Consensus at Scale: Multiple Awards, Testimonies & Reputation
14:43 Cannibalization on Third-Party Sources — On Purpose
15:07 Knowledge Graph: KG MID Confidence & Clarity Score
15:56 Visual Semantics Module & What's Next for the Course
16:24 Closing Thoughts

Get RankOS and the full AI search system 👉 https://www.skool.com/the-new-search/about

More SEO frameworks and breakdowns 👉 https://kasradash.com

A dentist blog post ranking for "does teeth whitening hurt" gets 15 visits a month. Bupa's teeth whitening service page, same subject, gets over 7,500.

That's the gap, and it's why half the sites I checked after the November core update are going backwards. Their pages drifted away from what the business actually sells.

Five steps to build a topical map properly, the two shortcuts that ruin one, and the type of topic you don't want Google connecting to your business at all.

Live examples in Ahrefs throughout, including a real practice's sitemap with 68 service pages and why copying it would be a mistake.

metadata.title: 14 How to Run a Competitor Content Gap Analysis by Silo (Floyi Tutorial)
metadata.author: Topical Authority SEO | Floyi
metadata.shortDescription:
Your Topical Authority Score shows where you stand across your whole map. Silo Analysis runs a competitor content gap analysis on each silo, so you see where you win, where you lose and the topics that close each gap.

In this tutorial, you'll learn how to:
- See your silos sorted into Leading, Contested, Opportunity, and Trailing
- Read each silo's Topical Authority Score, coverage and visibility
- Use Investment Priority to pick the silo to work on first
- Compare every tracked competitor silo by silo, in search results and in AI answers
- See who you're up against in one silo with the Competitor Leaderboard, including AI Overviews, AI Mode, Gemini, and ChatGPT
- Find the topics that close each gap, hub by hub
- Start a brief or a draft right from any gap

Floyi is the topical authority platform.
Start free: https://app.floyi.com/signup
Book a walkthrough for your team: https://tidycal.com/y/floyi-demo
Silo Analysis help doc: https://floyi.com/docs/tools/topical-authority-silo-analysis/
Next: Track the Prompts Your Buyers Ask AI https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WCFKLCDxX8w

Subscribe for practical SEO and AI search workflows.

Chapters:
0:00 What Silo Analysis tells you
0:15 Where Silo Analysis fits
0:34 Leading, Contested and Trailing
1:12 Your performance by silo
1:40 Investment Priority
2:15 Compare competitors by silo
2:49 Competitor Leaderboard
3:19 Hub Breakdown and content gaps
3:55 Act on a gap and keep it current

segments.text: Your topical authority score shows where

one silo at a time, and the topics that
close each gap. So the silo analysis tab

map and everything under it. The main

than spreading across all of them. Your
performance by silo gives each silo its

score for that silo alone. Coverage
counts the silo's topics where you rank
in the top 20. That's different from
pillar coverage on the scorecard, which
counts what you've published. Visibility
scores your rankings across the silo.
Higher positions count for more, and so
do the silo's most important topics.

to work on first. Contested silos come

focused push can flip them. Silos you

section.

strip.

domain by how many of the silo's topics
it covers in the top 20. It also shows
share of voice, average position, and
each domain's results in AI overviews,

is marked so you can see who's directly
above and below you. Hub breakdown and
content gaps splits the silo into its
hubs.
