and it's felt like it's impossible, it's
not because SEO is dead. It's because
you're targeting the wrong keywords.
Most beginners do one of two things.
They usually target huge keywords like
best laptops, or they pick random
keywords with zero traffic. Both
strategies fail. What's going on, guys?
My name is Kyle. In this video, I'm
going to show you exactly how to use
Semrush to find low competition keywords
that still get real traffic. Not theory,
not vague advice, actual filters, actual
steps, actual strategy. By the end of
this video, you'll know how to find easy
to rank keywords, validate traffic
potential, avoid impossible competition,
build topical authority, and create
content that ranks faster. Let's start
from the beginning what low competition
actually means. Before we open Semrush,
let's clear something up. Low
competition does not mean low search
volume. That's the mistake. You want low
key difficulty and decent traffic.
Keyword difficulty in Semrush is a score
from 0 to 100. Generally, 0 to 29 is
easy. 30 to 49 is possible. 50 to 69 is
hard, and 70 plus is very hard. If your
site is new, you want to mostly focus on
0 to 35. This is where small sites win.
Now, let's open Semrush. If you don't
have a Semrush account, you can create
one using the link in the description
below and get 14-day pro exclusive
access. Once inside Semrush, in the left
column below home, you'll magnifying
glass with a line going through it.
Scroll to the bottom and go to keyword
overview. Now, we don't type something
super specific. We start broad. If your
site is about fitness, web design, drop
shipping, WooCommerce, VPNs, or running
shoes, start with a general term. For
example, WooCommerce. So, in your search
bar, type WooCommerce, then click
search. Now, we're not going to target
this keyword. We're using it to explore.
Scroll down to keyword variations, and
then click view all keywords. This opens
the goldmine. Now, here's where the
magic happens. Once you're in, go to KD
percent and go down to custom range and
set it to 35. Then select apply. Then
volume, you want to set that minimum to
100. Then hit apply again. So, we have
volume 100 and KD 0 to 35%. This removes
useless zero traffic keywords. Now,
you're left with low competition and
real traffic. Already than 90% of
beginners, but we're not done. Now, sort
by volume descending. Look for keywords
that are four plus words long, sound
like real questions, and show buyer or
solving problem intent. For example,
instead of WooCommerce, you'll find how
to speed up WooCommerce checkout,
WooCommerce product page SEO tips, best
WooCommerce hosting for small store.
These are long-tail keywords. Long-tail
keywords have lower competition, convert
better, and rank faster. This is where
small websites win. Analyze search
intent. Click on one keyword and look at
intent. Semrush labels keywords as
informational, commercial, navigational,
and transactional. For new sites,
informational plus commercial are best.
Why? Because ranking for how to improve
WooCommerce speed is easier than ranking
for buy WooCommerce hosting. But, you
can still monetize informational
content. This is the my first strategy.
Teach first, monetize naturally. Now,
scroll down to SERP analysis. Look at
are the top results huge authority sites
or small niche blogs? Are there YouTube
videos ranking? And are forums like
Reddit ranking? If you see Reddit,
Quora, small blogs, or YouTube videos,
that means Google isn't fully satisfied.
That's opportunity. If you see Forbes,
HubSpot, Amazon, or massive e-commerce
giants, that's harder, but not always
impossible. Context matters. Now, let's
level up. In the left column, go to
keyword gap. Enter your website and two
to three competitors. Click compare and
now filter KD under 35, volume above
100. This shows keywords your
competitors rank for, but you don't.
This is one of the fastest ways to build
traffic. You're not guessing, you're
stealing proven opportunities. Now, go
to the keyword magic tool again and type
in your seed keyword again. Then towards
the top, next to all, you will see
questions. This shows how, what, why,
can, and best way to. Question keywords
are powerful because they're easier to
rank, they match search intent, and
they're perfect for blog content. For
example, how to reduce WooCommerce cart
abandonment, what is good keyword
difficulty in SEMrush, why is my product
page not ranking? These are
traffic-ready topics. Now, here's
something most beginners miss. Volume
alone isn't enough. Click a keyword.
Once you click that keyword, scroll down
to view SERP. Look at estimated traffic
of top pages. Sometimes a keyword says
200 searches per month, but the top
pages get 1,500 visits because it ranked
for 30 related keywords. This is called
topical clustering. That's the real
goal, not ranking for one keyword,
ranking for dozens. Inside the keyword
overview, look at the trend graph. Is it
stable, growing, or declining? Avoid
keywords that are trending down
long-term. Prefer evergreen stable
words. For my first style content, how
to, best tools, beginner guides, or
step-by-step, these stay relevant.
Instead of writing one article per
keyword randomly, group them. For
example, main topic, WooCommerce speed.
Cluster how to speed up WooCommerce
checkout, WooCommerce slow cart fix,
best catching plugin for WooCommerce,
and WooCommerce hosting comparison. Now,
create one main guide, three to four
supporting articles, and link them
together. Google sees topical authority,
and rankings improve faster. Some
keywords show KD 15, but when you check
SERP, all results are DR80+ domains.
Why? Because KD is an estimate. Always
manually check. If top 10 results have
weak backlinks, thin content, and
outdated info, that's opportunity. If
they're extremely strong pages, be
cautious. And if you want affiliate
revenue, filter by intent commercial,
then KD under 40. These are best top
review and comparison. For example, best
WooCommerce hosting for beginners, top
keyword research tools, and SEMrush
versus Ahrefs for small websites. These
convert extremely well. Once you find
good keywords, export them, put them
into a spreadsheet, create columns,
keywords, volume, KD, intent, and
content type. Now, prioritize. Lowest KD
plus highest volume plus strong intent.
This becomes your content roadmap. No
guessing, no random posting, just
strategic growth. How fast can you rank?
If your site is brand new, three to six
months. If it's an aged site, four to
eight weeks. And if it's an established
site, two to four weeks. Low competition
keywords rank faster because fewer
backlinks needed, less authority
required, and less content depth needed.
But consistency matters. Here's a bonus
strategy. Find weak pages to outrank.
Search your target keyword manually.
Click top three results. Ask, is this
article outdated? Is it too short? Is it
missing steps? And is it generic? If
yes, create something longer, clearer,
more step-by-step, and more
beginner-friendly. Google rewards
helpful content, not just big brands.
The secret is not finding one magical
keyword. It's finding 50 low competition
keywords and publishing consistently.
Traffic compounds, authority compounds,
and ranking compounds. Most people quit
too early. Here's a quick recap. Today
you learned how to use keyword magical
tool, filter by difficulty and volume,
analyze search intent, check SERP
manually, use keyword gap, find question
keywords, build clusters, validate
traffic potential, and avoid fake easy
keywords. This is how small websites
grow. Not by competing with the giants,

Using these links helps support the

free content just like this. If this
video helped, make sure to give it a

Thank you so much for watching, and I'll

metadata.author: Consumer Reviews
metadata.shortDescription:
Semrush vs Ahrefs: Explore SEO tools, data accuracy, pricing, and features to see which platform better fits your marketing needs.
💥 Affiliate Links Included👇
👉 Get Semrush ➜ https://trailgo.link/SJDEnrF

🔹 Our Commitment to Independence 🔹
HME Technology Corp maintains affiliate relationships with several of the brands featured on our channel. While we earn a commission if you purchase through our links (at no cost to you), our reviews remain completely independent. We base our recommendations entirely on our own research and testing to highlight what actually works best.

💼Business Inquiries: 
For sponsorships and collaborations, please contact us at 👉 partnerships@consumerreviews.me

Timestamp Sections: 
00:00 Intro
00:58 Semrush-How It Works
02:01 Ahrefs-How It Works
02:58 Semrush-Pricing & Features
03:38 Ahrefs-Pricing & Features
04:19 Real-World Scenarios
05:22 Final Verdicts
06:19 Outro

------------------------------------------------
Semrush – The Full Marketing Suite
------------------------------------------------

Semrush is designed to be more than just an SEO tool—it’s a complete digital marketing platform. From the moment you sign up, it walks you through setting up your first project, connecting Google Analytics, and tracking keywords. What really sets Semrush apart is how seamlessly it lets you move between tasks: keyword research, site audits, content planning, even social media and ad tracking. Once you get used to the slightly busy interface, it becomes a powerful workspace where you can manage everything under one roof. For agencies, SaaS companies, and e-commerce businesses that need to combine SEO with broader marketing campaigns, Semrush feels like the right choice because it doesn’t just show you the data—it helps you act on it.

------------------------------------------------
Ahrefs – Clean, Fast, and Focused
------------------------------------------------

Ahrefs takes a different approach, focusing purely on SEO with a streamlined interface and lightning-fast reports. Its Site Explorer is excellent for analyzing competitors, running backlink audits, and discovering keyword opportunities. If SEO is your main priority, Ahrefs delivers clean data and a smooth experience without distractions from extra tools you may not need. However, its narrow focus means you won’t get built-in content planning, ad tracking, or social media features, so it’s best suited for businesses or individuals who just want to dominate organic search and aren’t worried about tying SEO into a full marketing strategy.

------------------------------------------------
Pricing & My Recommendation
------------------------------------------------

Both Semrush and Ahrefs follow tiered pricing, with Semrush starting at $117/month (Pro) and scaling up to $416/month (Business), while Ahrefs starts at $129/month and goes up to $449/month (Advanced). Semrush gives you more flexibility and extra tools at similar price points, which is why I ended up preferring it for most of my clients. In real-world use, Ahrefs was amazing for competitor research and link-building, but Semrush helped me execute full campaigns—auditing sites, creating topic clusters, and tracking performance across multiple channels. Bottom line: if you just need raw SEO data, Ahrefs is a solid pick. But if you want to run a complete marketing strategy, Semrush gives you more control, more insight, and a better long-term value.

Hope you enjoyed my Semrush vs Ahrefs: I Used Both – Here's What You Need to Know Video.

metadata.title: New: Keyword Grouping in Keywords Explorer
metadata.author: Ahrefs Product Updates
metadata.shortDescription:
In this video, we’re introducing a new feature in Keywords Explorer: Keywords grouping. 
Subscribe ► https://www.youtube.com/AhrefsCom?sub_confirmation=1

***************************************
Additional Resources

Learn How to Do Effective Keyword Research for SEO ► https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLvJ_dXFSpd2tIF-QrFD854Mnb8D4Av5vx

Keyword Research Tutorial: From Start to Finish ►  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OMJQPqG2Uas

Keyword Research Tips to Help you Rank Higher in Google ►  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b7PzHO40bOU 

***************************************
It's always been pretty easy to find tons of keyword ideas in Keywords Explorer. All you have to do is enter a seed keyword and visit one of our reports.

However, with so many results, it used to take quite some time to filter through everything. This can be overwhelming. 

But you no longer have to do that anymore, because we’ve made keyword generation much easier with a new feature called keyword grouping. 

#keywordgrouping #keywordsexplorer #ahrefs

segments.text: Today I'm introducing our latest feature in Keywords Explorer: keyword grouping.
Let's do it!
[music]
It's always been pretty easy to find tons of keyword ideas in Keywords Explorer.
All you have to do is enter a seed keyword and visit one of our reports.
There's just one thing.
With so many results, it used to take quite some time to filter through everything and
things could get a bit overwhelming with the sheer amount of keyword ideas.
And not just that, but you'd also see many keywords that kind of have the same meaning,
but are worded differently.
Like "espresso machine" and "espresso maker."
They're pretty much the same thing, so it might feel noisy when doing topic research.
But you don't have to go through that anymore, because we've just made keyword generation
much easier with a new feature called keyword grouping.
Just click on either of these filters to group keywords by terms or by parent topic to
instantly organize that massive list of keywords into this list in the sidebar.
Plus, these numbers beside the groups tell you the total search volume that includes
the word or phrase in your target country.
It's definitely a much quicker way to sort through all your data.
Grouping by parent topic is a great way to see the most popular topics under a broad term.
For example, when it comes to espresso, we can tell just by scanning this list in the sidebar
that people are interested in espresso machines, specific brands like breville
and delonghi, espresso martinis, so on and so forth.
Click on a specific topic in the sidebar to zoom in on the topic and get ideas about
all the subtopics under it that we can potentially talk about.
So, imagine that we're researching coffee, and we see an interesting topic – "dalgona coffee."
Let's click on it in the sidebar and have a look at the results.
With this information, you can see that the main intent of "dalgona coffee"
is informational.
So we know that we should create a post on "how to make dalgona coffee."
And within the post, we could talk about what it is, where it's from, and of course,
how to make it.
We'd also want to describe things like how to make it with ground coffee.
So yea!
When doing keyword research with a broad seed, you can start by grouping by parent topic,
and then look at the sidebar to learn which specific topics that people are interested in.
Then, click on one of the parent topics to get ideas on the different kinds of subtopics
that you could cover for that parent topic.
That's not the only thing you can do.
We also have the "by terms" filter, which groups keywords by popular single-word terms.
This can be a really helpful way to dig deeper into a specific topic.
So let's say we're researching the query "best dog food."
There's quite a bit of search demand for this, but it also has a relatively high
keyword difficulty score.
So it's probably quite a tough topic to rank for.
But here's the trick.
More often than not, there are ways for us to attack broader topics like this from
a more specific angle.
So, if we check out this list of terms, they actually give us a look into the different
subtopics under the main topic.
For example, you'll see that people want to know about the best dry dog food, the best
dog food brands, the best dog food with or without grains, and the best dog food
for allergies... the list goes on.
Let's click on "allergies" to look at those keywords.
Scanning the list, we can see that this angle appears to be lower competition.
So have a think about whether your site is ready to compete with the bigger brands
that are ranking for the more competitive query, which in this case is "best dog food".
And if not, you might want to create a separate post targeting "best dog food for allergies" since
it's likely lower competition and it would serve an audience with a specific need.
And that's all!
Go try out these keyword groupings and let me know how it goes in the comments below.
Don't forget to subscribe to this channel for more product updates, tutorials, and
use cases, and of course like and share if you enjoyed this video.
See you in the next update! Bye!

वाला हूं एक कूपन कोड जिसके जरिए आपको और भी ज्यादा डिस्काउंट मिल जाएगा। सिंपली लिंक पे जैसे ही क्लिक करेंगे हम आ जाएंगे इनके होम पेज पे। हमें क्लिक करना होगा गेट स्टार्टेड बटन पे। हम गेट स्टार्टेड बटन पे क्लिक करेंगे एंड अपना डिटेल फटाफट यहां पे फिल कर लेते हैं। मैंने अपना डिटेल फटाफट फिल कर लिया है। एंड यहां पे आप देख सकते हैं मैंने जैसे ही डिटेल फिल कर लिया एंड उसके बाद मुझे यहां पे देखने को मिल सकता है एक्स्ट्रा 10% डिस्काउंट क्योंकि मैंने रेफरल लिंक से किया था। एंड सिंपली मैं एग्री कर लूंगा इसको एंड क्रिएट अकाउंट पे क्लिक कर दूंगा। जैसे ही मैं यहां पे क्लिक करूंगा आप देख सकते हैं एक ईमेल जो है वह मेरी ईमेल पे आ गया है। मुझे सिंपली ईमेल पे क्लिक करके वेरीफाई करना होगा। तो मैं फटाफट ईमेल को ओपन कर लेता हूं। समटाइ जो मेल है वह स्पैम फोल्डर में आ जाता है। तो आप ध्यान दीजिएगा एक बार स्पैम फोल्डर जरूर चेक कर लीजिएगा एंड यहां से मार्क कर दीजिएगा रिपोर्ट नॉट स्पैम। इसके बाद आपको हर बार जो भी मेल आएगा वो डायरेक्टली इनबॉक्स पे आने लग जाएगा। एंड अभी हम क्लिक करेंगे वेरीफाई ईमेल पे। हमने जैसे ही वेरीफाई ईमेल पे क्लिक किया। अभी आप देख सकते हैं हमारा जो ईमेल है वो सक्सेसफुली वेरीफाई हो चुका है। एंड अब हम अपना अकाउंट को लॉगिन कर लेते हैं फटाफट। देख सकते हैं अभी हमने अकाउंट को लॉग इन कर लिया है। एंड यहां पर कोई भी प्लान एक्टिव नहीं है। हम फटाफट आ जाएंगे शॉप पेज पे। एंड शॉप पेज पर आने के बाद यहां पर आपको मल्टीपल प्लान देखने को मिल जाएगा। सिमरस सिमरस विद साइड ऑट एचएफ के चार प्लान आपको देखने को मिल जाएंगे अलग-अलग के साथ। आपकी इच्छा है आप जिस प्लान को लेना चाहते हैं। आप यह ध्यान रखिएगा यहां पर आपको 1 मंथ, 3 मंथ, 6 मंथ एंड 12 मंथ में देखने को मिल जाएगा। अगर आप 3 मंथ का लेते हैं तो बाय डिफ़ॉल्ट आपको 7% का डिस्काउंट मिल जाएगा। 6 मंथ पे आपको 10% का प्राइिंग पे डिस्काउंट मिलेगा। वन मंथ के अकॉर्डिंग एंड 12 मंथ पे आपको 20% का डिस्काउंट मिल जाएगा इन कंपैरिजन ऑफ़ वन मंथ। मैं यहां पे आपको एक कूपन कोड भी देने वाला हूं। जिस कूपन कोड का आप इस्तेमाल करके एक्स्ट्रा डिस्काउंट ले सकते हैं। अगर आप फर्स्ट मंथ के लिए बाय करना चाहते हैं तो आप कूपन कोड यूज़ कर सकते हैं। एन ईw यानी कि न्यू 10 न्यू 10 का इस्तेमाल करने से आपको 10% का एक्स्ट्रा डिस्काउंट और देखने को मिल जाएगा। मैं यहां पे 3 मंथ्स के लिए बाय करने वाला हूं। मैं सिंपली 3 मंथ्स को सेलेक्ट करूंगा। एंड यहां पे सब्सक्राइब नाउ पे क्लिक कर दूंगा क्योंकि मैं यहां पे सिमरस और एचएफ दोनों का प्लान बाय करने वाला हूं। एंड जैसे ही मैं 3 मंथ के लिए सेलेक्ट करूंगा, आप यहां पे देख सकते हैं मेरे को 7% का एक्स्ट्रा डिस्काउंट देखने को मिल चुका है। एंड सिंपली मैं एग्री पे क्लिक करूंगा एंड यहां पे एक कूपन कोड डालूंगा न्यू 20। यह 3 मंथ, 6 मंथ एंड 12 मंथ के लिए एप्लीकेबल है यह कूपन कोड। एंड सिंपली मैं अप्लाई पे क्लिक करूंगा। जैसे ही अप्लाई पे क्लिक करूंगा, आप यहां पे देख सकते हैं जो इसकी प्राइजिंग है ₹1783 हो चुकी है। मैं सिंपली एग्री पे क्लिक करके यहां पे प्लेस ऑर्डर पे क्लिक कर दूंगा। जैसे ही मैं प्लेस ऑर्डर पे क्लिक करूंगा, ध्यान रखिएगा मैंने metadata.title: Internal Linking Strategy: How to Set it Up
metadata.author: Semrush
metadata.shortDescription:
In this video, you'll learn how to set up a basic internal linking strategy, and some mistakes to avoid. 🚀 Keep learning with our FREE SEO courses ►  https://smr.sh/KNb

Internal linking is maybe one of the most underutilized search engine optimization techniques by SEOs and developers alike. Have no fear, though! Solid internal linking is actually much easier than you might think. 

Just like we talked about in our recent Top 5 SEO mistakes video, it really is a matter of investing a few minutes and doing the basics really well.

Step one: You’ll want to identify the pages of yours that target high volume keywords and then develop them as what we’ll call “hub pages.” For our site, we could set up hub pages for cakes, donuts, pastries, pies, and breads as the hubs. You’ll want to avoid picking too many hub pages. Keep them to the essentials. (and I think we have all the essentials right here)

Next, map out what fits under each hub page. Under the Cakes hub page, for example, you could have birthday cakes, graduation cakes, wedding cakes, company event cakes, or even funny cakes that make you smile. 

Third, you’ll want to consider setting up one more level below each of these clusters. Under birthday cakes, for example, you could set up sub categories such as “cakes for kids” and “cakes for adults” - or it could be “whole wheat” and “gluten free” under your bread hubs. Just think through your products and audiences to segment these the best way.

Next - you might need to bribe your dev folks with some donuts for this next step. This hierarchy should become the basis for your main Navigational Internal Links - also known as the “Nav Bar.” If this isn’t the case, work with the dev team to make sure your site’s navigation actually aligns with these hubs and clusters. 

The fifth and final prep step is tackling Contextual Internal Links. What are we talking about here? Contextual internal links are typically placed within the main body content of a page and is important because it helps users find additional related information they may need. Plus, internal links also pass authority to the page you’re linking to and helps search engines understand your site. Remember Google is always crawling your site and you want to help the machines really understand everything about it!

You’re not alone in doing this, though. SEMrush has great tools to help you do all of this well.

The easiest way to audit your internal links is to jump into the SEMRush Internal Linking report in Site Audit. It quickly shows the strongest and weakest links on the site. 

Use this to identify errors, warnings, and notices regarding your site’s internal links and make the suggested changes to your site. It’s THAT simple!

We all know that backlinks are valuable to improve your Google rankings. But it’s tough getting them.

So that’s why internal links are something worth looking into. You have 100% control over them and they can be used to pass PageRank to your pages, effectively boosting rankings. 

By strategically building the authority of a page through multiple internal links, you can significantly enhance the rankings of other important pages on your website.

In this video, we delve into the three key ingredients that make this strategy work:

► Backlinks to the linking page which contribute to a page's authority, also known as PageRank.
► Matching searcher intent: it's important to align your page's content with the intent of searchers.
► Competing against manageable competitors: choose competitors that are realistically within reach and share a similar level of authority.

Next, we guide you through the process of finding internal link opportunities. We suggest creating a list of important pages on your website that you want to rank higher in Google, based on their business value and traffic potential.

We provide three methods to discover relevant pages to link from: site search in Google, Ahrefs' Site Audit, and the Best By Links report in Ahrefs' Site Explorer. Finally, we recommend tracking your keywords using a rank tracking tool to assess the impact of internal links on your rankings. 

Internal linking isn't solely about passing PageRank but also enhances user experience by providing visitors with relevant resources. While internal links are powerful, other strategies such as acquiring external backlinks or updating content may be necessary for significant ranking improvements.

its so-called "authority."

effectively boosting their Google rankings.
Now, there are three things that make this strategy work.
The first is backlinks to the linking page.
Backlinks are essentially what fuel's a page's so-called "authority" or what's more officially
called PageRank.
And when a page has gotten quality backlinks, it's able to pass a portion of its PageRank to
the URLs it links to.
Now, if a page doesn't have much "authority", then it can't help boost a page's rankings
because there's nothing really to pass.
The second requirement to make this strategy work is to ensure the linked page matches
searcher intent.

In this video, you’ll learn how to use internal links to rank higher in Google. 

***************************************
Additional Link Building Resources

SEO For Beginners: A Basic Search Engine Optimization Tutorial for Higher Google Rankings ► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DvwS7cV9GmQ

Content Hubs: Where SEO and Content Marketing Meet ► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nIbJI1kCxrU 

Ahrefs Webmaster Tools (AWT) - Our Free SEO Tool ► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ipTk-qGrNlc 

Link Building for Beginners: Complete Guide to Get Backlinks in 2020 ► https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=C5ddo63kHHI 

Link Building Tutorials (Step-By-Step) ► https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLvJ_dXFSpd2tjUTuAHpHidz5e2hAedP_m 

Link Building Case Study (SEO Stats Post) ► https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLvJ_dXFSpd2u_ABxIRO6RVK3ucKyzn96Y 

***************************************
Internal links are simply links from one page to another on the same website. And they’re important for 3 main reasons. 

► They help search engines like Google discover new pages so they can be added to their index. 
► Internal links help pass PageRank around your site, effectively “powering” other pages.
► Internal links help search engines to better understand what a page is about. They do this by looking at anchor texts and the text that surrounds the link.

So, knowing these three things, here’s how you can boost your rankings with internal links. 

The first way is to create a logical hierarchy in your site structure. 

Think of site structure as a mindmap. At the top, you’d have your homepage. Then you’d probably have main topics that branch out from your homepage like your services page, your blog, and about page. 

Then from these main topics, you have even more branches to other pages. 

Structure helps search engines to understand the relationship between these pages, where branches are created using internal links. 

And you can leverage this by using an internal linking strategy called content hubs.

We’ll show you how it works in this video.  

The third way is to use the Link Opportunities report in Ahrefs’ Site Audit. 

All you have to do is sign up for a FREE Ahrefs Webmaster Tools account, verify your site, and then you can run a free website audit. After your audit is complete, head on over to the Link Opportunities report. 

This report shows you internal linking opportunities based on keywords your pages rank for. 

Another method is to look at your site’s power pages. 

Naturally, some pages will earn more links than others. So they have more so-called “authority” they can pass to other pages on your website. 

You’ll learn how to leverage power pages to boost your rankings in this video. 

Whichever method you decide to use, the most important thing to remember is that you don’t need to force internal links. So don’t link from irrelevant pages and don’t overdo it.

metadata.author: Chris Palmer SEO
metadata.shortDescription:
On Page SEO Internal Linking Tips Learn To Improve On Site SEO For Your Website. Chris Palmer SEO: https://chrispalmer.org

In this on page SEO tips training, I will walk you through the often-overlooked power of internal backlinks and how addressing link deficits can provide a massive ranking advantage in some of the most competitive digital landscapes in Google and other search engines. 

If you are a small business owner or a seasoned SEO pro, understanding that internal links are your way of telling Google which pages are the most important is foundational to your long-term SEO success. 

I share actionable internal linking tips, practical tips on page SEO—from checking your profile for free in Google Search Console ( GSC ) to utilizing advanced "hidden" internal linking SEO strategies including the on site jump links and the no-index follow pages strategy. 

On Site Internal Linking Tips:
Google Search Console is Essential: Google explicitly outlines "Top Linked Pages" in Search Console because internal link volume is a primary signal of page importance.

* Internal vs. External Votes
While external links show what the world thinks of you, internal links are what you tell Google about your own hierarchy and authority.

* Keyword Set Optimization
A single page ranks for many terms; your internal anchor text should mirror the term variations (LSI, entities, and co-occurring phrases) used by top-ranking competitors.

* Site-Wide Density Matters
 It isn’t just about links to one page; the overall anchor text density across your entire site tells Google the "category" and "topic" of your business.

* Hidden Tactics
 High-level competitors often use "jump links" or "follow, no-index" pages to build massive internal keyword density without cluttering the user experience.

* Match and Mirror
 Analyze the winners in your SERP to see their internal link ratios and anchor text variety, then match those "deficits" to climb the ladder.

metadata.title: Your Best Pages Are Invisible to Google — Internal Linking Explained (2026)
metadata.author: Abdul Latif
metadata.shortDescription:
Your best pages are already on your website. Google just can't find them.

In almost every website I audit, I find the same hidden problem: important pages that are live, that the owner paid to create — and that Google has barely ever visited. Not because the content is bad. Because nothing links to them.

Google discovers your pages by following links. A page with no internal links pointing to it is a room in a house with no door: it exists, but nobody can reach it. And the buried pages are usually the money pages — the service pages and city pages that actually bring enquiries.

In this video I walk through the 5 internal linking fixes I use on real websites:
1. Link from your strongest pages to your money pages
2. Use anchor text that says what the page is about ("click here" tells Google nothing)
3. Fix the orphan pages — every important page needs at least one internal link
4. Don't link everything to everything — 5 deliberate links beat 50 random ones
5. Re-check your internal links after every redesign

Internal linking costs nothing: no ads, no new content, no backlinks to buy. It is simply making sure the good work you already did can actually be found.

I am Abdul Latif, an SEO Specialist with 2 years of hands-on experience in Technical, On-Page and Local SEO. I do SEO audits and WordPress technical fixes — if you want me to look at your website and tell you which of your pages are buried, send me a message or comment your website below.

0:44 — Why publishing more content does not fix it

2:00 — The money pages are the buried ones
2:32 — Fix 1 — Link your strongest pages to your money pages
3:09 — Fix 2 — Anchor text that describes the page
3:44 — Fix 3 + 4 — Fix orphans; do not link everything
4:19 — Fix 5 — Re-check links after every redesign + recap

metadata.title: The First Rule of Internal Linking (That Most SEOs Ignore)
metadata.author: Edward Sturm
metadata.shortDescription:
E1013: Breaking down a simple but widely misunderstood idea in SEO: internal links are not “set and forget.”

Most people treat internal linking as something you do once when you publish a page. David argues the opposite. If you are not revisiting and adjusting your internal links regularly, you are likely wasting authority and slowing down your ability to rank new pages.

The core idea is straightforward: internal links only matter when they come from pages that actually have authority. And the only reliable way to get that authority is by ranking and getting clicks. That means your internal linking strategy should evolve as your pages start to perform.

This conversation covers how to think about internal links as an investment, how to use ranking pages to lift other pages, and why adding more links is often the wrong move.

What we cover:
- Why internal links are not “free authority”
- The real role of ranking pages in passing value to other pages
- Why blog posts that don’t rank don’t help your money pages
- How to use internal links to move pages from “almost ranking” to page one
- When to remove or reduce internal links without hurting rankings
- Why automated internal linking tools can cause more harm than good
- How to identify pages that are close to ranking using Search Console
- The concept of topical authority and how it develops across a group of pages
- How to think about internal links like an expense account, not an unlimited resource
- Why too many links on a page can dilute impact instead of helping

Key takeaway:

This internal linking hack is not about linking everything together. It is about directing authority from pages that are already working to pages that are close to working. That requires ongoing adjustments, not a one-time setup.

If you treat your site like a system, where pages earn authority and then pass it on strategically, you can rank new content faster without relying entirely on backlinks.

Subscribe to this channel now: https://www.youtube.com/c/clickminded?sub_confirmation=1

Internal linking is one of the most powerful—but most neglected—SEO strategies. In this video, I’ll show you the exact system I use to boost rankings fast with AI-powered internal linking in 5 minutes or less using ClickMinded’s Project Agent.

The Internal Linking Problem:
❌ Manually auditing links page by page is painful
❌ Internal links are often ignored or done incorrectly
❌ Agencies waste hours cleaning up past SEO mistakes
❌ No scalable system for finding new opportunities

What You’ll Learn:
✅ How to use the ClickMinded Project Agent with your XML sitemap
✅ How AI instantly identifies internal linking opportunities
✅ How to get anchor text recommendations grouped by source page
✅ How to integrate internal linking into your SEO strategy
✅ How to save hours of manual SEO work with automation

Key Resources Covered:
📝 Project Agent workflow for internal linking
📝 SOPs for SEO audits and on-page optimization
📝 Example XML sitemap integration

Perfect For:
🙋‍♂️ SEO specialists who need scalable workflows
🙋‍♂️ Agencies optimizing multiple client websites
🙋‍♂️ Consultants offering quick-win SEO improvements
🙋‍♂️ Teams looking to boost rankings without new content

The 5-Step Process:
1️⃣ Add business + website context to the Project Agent
2️⃣ Upload your XML sitemap or URL list
3️⃣ Ask for internal linking opportunities by keyword/topic
4️⃣ Review AI-generated anchor text + link suggestions
5️⃣ Implement changes and track SEO performance

🎯 Challenge: Take your site (or a client’s), upload the sitemap, and see how quickly you can uncover dozens of high-value internal linking opportunities with AI.

videos.full_text: আজকে আর কিছু নিয়ে কথা হবে না। শুধুমাত্র ক্রোল স্ট্যাটাস এবং ক্রোল স্ট্যাটাস ভেতরে এমনভাবে ঢুকবে যে কোনদিন কনফিউজড হবেন না যে কোন ক্লায়েন্ট ক্রোল বাজেট নিয়ে যা কিছু আসক করুক না কেন পারফেক্টলি আনসার দিতে পারবেন। আজকে এই যে ক্রোল স্ট্যাটাস আছে এই ক্রোল স্ট্যাটাস নিয়ে কথা বলব। কতবার রিকোয়েস্ট করে ক্রোল বাজেট কাদের দরকার কিভাবে অপটিমাইজ করতে পারেন ইন ডিটেইলস সবকিছু। 10 থেকে 15 রিকোয়েস্ট হচ্ছে। আপনি দেখবেন এখানে এসে আজকে যদি আমি ক্লিক করি আজকে হল জুন 217 বার রিকোয়েস্ট পাঠাইছে। আমার এই পেইজের সংখ্যাই হল 200র মত। 250র মত। লবি গুড। এখানে দেখেন 418 বার। দট মিন্স একটা পেইজ দুইবারের উপর ট্রল হয়েছে। তো ইসু নাই। [নাক ডাকা] কতগুলা ক্রোল রিকোয়েস্ট হচ্ছে এটা একটা ইস্যু দেখবেন কোন রেসপন্স কোড কতবার আছে কতবার রেসপন্স হচ্ছে ওকে স্ট্যাটাস কোড আমি আগে ভিডিও দিছি এগুললা দেখবেন ওকে স্ট্যাটাস কোড হলো 200 দ্যাট মিন্স আমার সার্ভার ঠিকঠাকভাবে পেইজগুলাকে রেসপন্স করছে যখন গুগল ক্রোল করতে আসছে নট ফাউন্ড মানে করতে খুঁজে পাচ্ছে না আমাদের আদার যে ইস্যুগুলো আসছে এগুলা দেখবেন কোন ফাইল টাইপ বেশি ক্রোল হচ্ছে এটা কি সিএসএস এইচটিএম জাভাস্ক্রিপ্ট নাকি অন্য কোন ক্রল রেসপন্স টাইম যত যত কম হবে তত বেটার ঠিক আছে যত তাড়াতাড়ি রেসপন্স করবে যদি দেখেন প্রচুর পরিমাণফ এর আছে আছে ফাইভ এক্সেস এরর আছে তখন আপনি স্টেপ নিবেন কিভাবে স্টেপ নিবেন সাবস্ক্রাইব না করলে করে রাখেন ভিডিও তো অবশ্যই আসবে ঠিক আছে সেকেন্ড [নাক ডাকা] হলো এইচটিএমএল পেইজ যদি কম থাকে প্যারামিটার ইউআরএল বা ইউজলেস প্যাটারন যদি বেশি থাকে তাহলে আপনার এই সমস্যাটা আসে ক্রল টুলারস আছে ধরেন আমাদের স্ক্রিমিং ফক দিয়ে আমি ওদি স্যামরাস দিয়ে দেখাইছি আপনি এটা দিয়ে ফুল ক্রোল করেও এই জিনিসটা বুঝতে পারেন আমার জন্য মনে হয় গুগল সার্চ কনসোল ইজ মোর দেন ইনাফ আমি আশা করি এই জিনিসটা আপনারা পুরোপুরি বুঝতে পারছেন। এখন হৃদয় ভাই ক্রোল বাজেটযে কোন কোন জায়গায় মূলত নষ্ট হয় আপনার এক্সপেরিয়েন্স অনুযায়ী প্রথমত আপনার যদি ফ্যাক্টেড নেভিগেশন ফিল্টার থাকে। ঠিক আছে? এই জিনিসগুলা আপাতত শিখে রাখেন। আমি প্র্যাক্টিক্যালি আপনাদের দেখাবো। ইন্টার্নাল সার্চ রেজাল্ট পেইজ থাকে। ইন্টার্নাল সার্চ রেজাল্ট পেজ হলো যখন আমাদের সার্চ করে কেউ সার্চ করার পরেই দেখবেন একটা সার্চ নামে এরকম আমাদের যদি Amazজন এ যাই এরকম সার্চ নামে একটা পেইজ ক্রিয়েট হয়ে যায়। এই আননেসেসারি পেইজের জন্য। আমাদের ট্যাগ আছে। ঠিক আছে? আমরা যদি এখানে স্মল সাইমিং দেই তাহলে এখানে দেখবেন অনেকগুলা ট্যাগ থাকে। এই ট্যাগগুলা নিয়েও অনেক সময় অনেকগুলা পেইজ ক্রিয়েট হয়ে যায়। এই পেইজগুলো এইযে দেখেন আমি যতটুকু ক্লিক করছি ততটুকু নতুন নতুন পেইজ ক্রিয়েট হচ্ছে। সফটফর ব্রোকেন পেইজ যদি থাকে এর আগের ক্লাসে দেখাইছি আপনার যদি রিডাইরেক্ট চেইন থাকে। রিডাইরেক্ট চেইন হলো ধরেন আপনি একটা ইউআরএল এর সাথে অলরেডি রিডাইরেক্ট করছেন। ধরেন আপনার একটা ইউআরএল হলো এ। আপনি এর সাথে বির রিডাইরেক্ট করলেন। তারপরে আপনার মনে হলো বির সাথে আপনি সি এর করবেন। সি এর সাথে আপনি ডি করবেন। এটা কিন্তু আপনার একটা একটার বদলে চারটা হোপ হয়ে গেছে। এর বদলে আপনি এর সাথে বরাবর ডি এর একটা রিডাইরেক্ট করে দিতে পারেন। তখন এই রিডাইরেক্ট চেইনটা স্মুথ হয়ে যাবে এবং আপনার এখানে টাইম খরচ হবে না। ডুপ্লিকেট কন্টেন্ট যদি থাকে তাহলে উইদাউট আপনি একই টাইপের একই কন্টেক্সট এর জন্য Googleুগল কে টাইম নষ্ট করাচ্ছেন। তারপরে আপনার যদি এক্সএমএল সাইট ম্যাপ ব্লোডেড থাকে নো ইন্ডেক্স দিয়েফর ইরর দিয়ে রিডাইরেক্ট দিয়ে তখন কিন্তু আপনার কি হবে এবং নট দ লিস্ট সার্ভারে যদি কোন ধরনের সমস্যা থাকে তাও কিন্তু আপনার ক্রোল বাজেট নষ্ট হয় অপ্রয়োজনীয় পেইজে বট সিম্পল ভাবে আপনি কিভাবে ক্রোল করবেন ফিল্টার ইউআরএল আছে ইন্টারনাল সার্চ আছে কার্ড চেকআউট এডমিন এগুলাকে ব্লক করে রাখবেন সবসময় ঠিক আছে আমি আপনাদের গত ক্লাসের এর আগের ক্লাসের ভিডিওতে পুরো জিনিসটা দেখাই এখন [নাক ডাকা] যদি বলেন যে ভাই কিভাবে করবো একটা এক্সাম্পল দেই আপনি আপনার যদি ই-কমার্স ওয়েবসাইট থাকে ঠিক আছে শিখে রাখেন এখানে যাবেন যাওয়ার পরে আমি এটা এটা দেখায় শেষ করে দিব ভাই খুব বেশি সময় নিব না বিকজ নট ইম্পর্টেন্ট ফর আস এখনকার সময় আপনারা যারা নতুন আছেন এগুলা নিয়ে কি করে না এজন্য আমার এই ক্লাসগুলা নিতে সবসময় ভয় হয় যে আপনারা বুঝতে পারেন কিনা জানাবেন ভাই আমি এর চেয়ে সহজ করে আমি এক্সপ্লেইন করার মতো পাই নাই ধরেন এটা আমার রোবটটি এখন আমাদের ইউজার যে এজেন্ট সেম থাকবে এখানে এখানে ডিজেলা যে আছে ঠিক আছে আমি সিম্পল ভাবে কোড লিখবো কিভাবে কোড লেখবো ঠিক আছে শিখে রাখেন এচবিটা তো আছে ডিজেলাওতে দেবেন এ ডিজেলাতে গিয়ে প্রথমত ব্লক করবেন এই সার্চ বেচারারে ঠিক আছে যতগুলা সার্চ আসবে এগুলা তারপরে আমি ডিজেলাও সেম থাকবে ঠিক আছে ডিজে কিন্তু সেইম থাকবে এখানে ডিজে লিখবেন লিখার পরে আমার যে কার্ড আছে আমি এই কার্ডটাকে করব ঠিক আছে কার্ডের আগে এরকম কি থাকবে আমার যে কার্ড পেইজ আছে এগুলা কিন্তু পেইজের নাম তারপরে আমার ডিজে সেম থাকবে এবং ডিজেল আওয়ার সাথে কি থাকবে? ভেরি গুড। আমাদের যে চেক আউট আছে এই চেক আউট গুলাকে এর আগে পেজে সিম্বল থাকবে। বলে দিচ্ছি। তারপরে আমাদের যে ডবলিউপি এডমিন আছে ডবলিউপি এডমিন পেজ থাকবে। ডবলিউপি এডমিন থাকবে। তারপর আমাদের কি থাকবে? আমাদের এরকম ধরনের সোর যে পেজগুলো আছে সোর পেজগুললা থাকবে। তারপরে সেশন আইডি যেগুলো আছে এগুলাকে আপনি ব্লক করে রাখতে পারেন। সিম্পল। মাথায় থাকলেই হইছে। আর আননেসেসারি ভাবে রাখবেন না। আপনাদের যে কম পেইজের যে ওয়েবসাইটগুলো আছে এই ওয়েবসাইটগুলাকে সবসময় কি করবেন? এমন পেইজ আপনি ব্লক করবেন না পাকমি করতে গিয়ে যেটার দরকার আছে। ঠিক আছে? তো আশা করি আমি আপনাদের পুরোপুরি বুঝাইতে পারছি ক্রোল বাজেট অপটিমাইজেশন জিনিসটা কি এবং ক্রোল বাজেট জিনিসটা কি? যদি তারপরেও হেজিটেশন থাকে আমাকে জানাবেন। জাস্ট একটা জিনিস ক্লিয়ার হবেন। আমাদের যে লোকাল ওয়েবসাইটগুলো আছে লেস দেন 1থাউজ পেইজের ওয়েবসাইটগুলো আছে আই ডোন্ট নিড টু থিংক এবাউট ইট। আমার সাইট ম্যাপ ক্লিন থাকলে রোবট যদি ঠিকঠাক ভাবে আসে আমার যদি রেগুলার ক্রল হয় দে উইল বি ওকে। আর যদি না হয় তাহলে তো সমস্যা আছে। ওকে থ্যাংক ইউ সো মাচ। ইনশআল্লাহ নেক্সট ভিডিওতে আবার দেখা হবে। আসসালামু আলাইকুম।

metadata.title: Crawl Budget and the Crawl Stats report - Google Search Console Training
metadata.author: Google Search Central
metadata.shortDescription:
Daniel Waisberg comes back for a special episode of Google Search Console Training. He provides a short introduction to how Google crawls pages, and defines terms such as crawl rate, crawl demand, and crawl budget. Then he dives into the new Crawl Stats report in Search Console which provides data on crawl requests, average response time, and more.

Search Console Crawl Stats report → http://goo.gle/3aLcUOa
What Crawl Budget Means for Googlebot →  http://goo.gle/3shjGAR

segments.text: DANIEL WAISBERG: Hi, I'm Daniel Waisberg,
Search Advocate at Google.
And today I'll provide a short introduction
to how Google crawls pages, and provide definitions
for terms such as crawl rate, crawl demand, and crawl budget.
Then I'll dive into the Search Console Crawl Stats
report, which provides data on crawl
requests, average response time, and more.
The report contains information for several Google crawlers,
but I'll focus on the search aspect of it.
As a disclaimer, this presentation
will be more relevant if you work with a large website.
If you have a site with fewer than a few thousand pages,
you do not need to worry about it.
But if you ask me, never hurts to learn something new.
Who knows, your site may become the next big thing.
[MUSIC PLAYING]
The crawling process begins with a list of web addresses
from [? best ?] crawls and site maps provided by site owners.
Google uses the web crawlers to visit these addresses,
read the information in them, and follow links
on those pages.
The crawlers will revisit pages already
in the list to check if they have changed,
and also crawl new pages it discovered.
During this process, the crawlers
have to make important decisions,
such as prioritizing when and what to crawl,
while making sure the website can handle the server requests
made by Google.
Crawl demand is how much the content is desired by Google.
It is affected by URLs that haven't been crawled
by Google before, and by Google's estimation
on how often content changes on the non-URLs.
The successfully crawled pages are processed and passed
to Google indexing to prepare the content for serving
on Google Search results.
Google wants to make sure that it
doesn't overload your servers, as a good citizen would do.
With that in mind, Google computes your site crawl rate,
which represents the maximum number
of concurrent connections a crawler may
use to crawl your site.
This value is calculated by Google periodically based
on your site's responsiveness--
or in other words, how much crawling traffic it can handle.
If the site is quick and consistent to respond
to crawlers, the rate goes up if there is demand from indexing.
If the site slows down or responds with server errors,
the rate goes down and Google crawls less.
In rare cases, where Google crawlers overload your servers,
you can set a crawl rate limit using the crawl rate settings
report in Search Console.
Taking crawl rate and crawl demand together,
we can define crawl budget as the number of URLs Google
can and wants to crawl.
My colleague [INAUDIBLE] wrote a detailed blog post

To find out how often Google crawls your site
and what the responses were, you should use the Search Console
Crawl Stats report, which provides
statistics about Google's crawling behavior.
Here are some questions you can answer with the data provided.
What's your site's general availability?
What's the average page response for a crawl request?
And how many requests were made by Google
to your site in the last 90 days?
Let's dive in to learn more about the report.
Log in to Search Console and find
the Settings page, where you can open the Crawl Stats report.
Know that this report is only available for properties
at the domain level.
It is not available for properties that include
[INAUDIBLE].
In the summary page, you'll find a lot of information.
The main elements are the crawling trends chart,
the host status details, and the crawl request breakdown.
The chart shows the trends for three metrics.
The total crawl request for URLs on your site,
whether successful or not.
Request resources hosted outside of your site are not counted.
So if your images are served on another domain,
such as a content delivery network or CDN,
they will not appear here.
The total download size from your site during crawling.
If Google casts a page resource that is used by multiple pages,
the resource is only requested the first time.
And the average page response time for a crawl
request to retrieve the page content.
This metric does not include retrieving page resources
such as scripts, images, and other
linked or embedded content.
The response time does not account
for page rendering time.
Look for major spikes, drops, and trends
over time in your data.
For example, if you see a significant drop in total crawl
requests, make sure no one added a new robots.txt to your site.

all the requests.

in average response time.

metadata.title: Using Log File Analysis to Improve How Google Crawls My Website
metadata.author: TM Blast
metadata.shortDescription:
Understanding how Google crawls your website is achieved through log file analysis. Log file analysis takes the raw logs from your server (for me, it is my cpanel) and then throws them into Screaming Frog to analyze the data. From there, I like to see the number of events that Google has on my site, which shows what pages they have crawled. 

In my video, I had just under 900 unique events, which doesn't mean anything on the surface. However, I saw that my blogs were making up around 25% of that activity, which was alarming since most of my blogs were back from 2015 and had zero importance to what I was doing today. Another 15% (maybe closer to 20%) of my crawl was wasted on WordPress plugins that don't need to be crawled. 

Therefore, by removing those blog posts, which I did on 12-18-2023, and blocking the paths in the robots.txt file, I'm giving Google about 50% more guidance on where I want them to crawl on my site. In this case, I want them to crawl my service pages because Google has only crawled them once or twice in about a month, helping them get indexed.

Are you interested in a Free SEO Audit for your website? https://www.tmblast.com/services/free-seo-audit/

Want to learn more about Greg Kristan from TM Blast? https://www.tmblast.com/about-this-site/greg/

Are you interested in having me work on your SEO Strategy? If so, visit the site and fill out the form!
https://www.tmblast.com/

metadata.title: Log Files Don't Lie: A 30-Day Crawl Analysis That Changed How We Prioritize Technical SEO
metadata.author: brightonSEO
metadata.shortDescription:
Recorded at brightonSEO October 2026.

In this talk, John will reveal how to tap into the most accurate SEO data available, your server logs, without needing an enterprise budget or expensive software. He will guide attendees through a real enterprise log analysis project, focusing on actionable use cases like bot segmentation, crawl frequency patterns, and identifying the most common anomalies that signal major structural flaws. Attendees will leave with a clear, step-by-step playbook and a ready-to-use template for presenting meaningful, undeniable insights directly to their engineering teams.

For more information about brightonSEO and to get tickets, visit www.brightonseo.com

SUBSCRIBE for more videos: https://www.youtube.com/channel/brightonSEO?sub_confirmation=1

************************************************************************

Follow us...
Twitter: https://www.twitter.com/brightonSEO
LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/brightonseo
Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/brightonseo

************************************************************************

brightonSEO is the biggest search marketing conference in the world and takes place in the UK and US. We give away thousands of free tickets every year and we’d love to see you there. As well as running one of the world’s most popular search marketing conferences we also organise practical, hands-on and in-depth analytics, PPC, SEO training courses – so you can up-skill in a specific area of search marketing.

Find out out more at brightonseo.com

metadata.title: Should I worry about crawl budget? | Search Off the Record
metadata.author: Google Search Central
metadata.shortDescription:
There is a lot of confusion around crawl budget so Martin, Lizzi, and Gary from Search Relations are here to bring clarity for everyone unsure about it. Are you worried about your website not being crawled quickly? Not sure what consumes and wastes your crawl budget? Learn when you should and shouldn’t be worried about your crawl budget. This episode covers misconceptions and frequently asked questions concerning crawl budget.  

Resources: 
What Crawl Budget Means for Googlebot → https://goo.gle/3pIwXTM 

Episode transcript → http://goo.gle/sotr045-transcript

Search Off the Record is a podcast series that takes you behind the scenes of Google Search with the Search Relations team.

Subscribe to Google Search Central Channel → https://goo.gle/SearchCentral

 #SOTRpodcast #Search

metadata.title: Crawl Budget, Explained: What Eats It and How to Get More
metadata.author: Misha Manko
metadata.shortDescription:
Crawl budget is the number of URLs Google can and wants to crawl on your site. Google says 90% of sites don’t need to worry about it. On the sites I work with, it starts to matter from about 100 pages.

In this video: the two parts of crawl budget (capacity limit and crawl demand), how crawling actually works, what eats the budget, what works and what doesn’t, how to get more, diagnostics in four steps, what changed in 2026, and how AI bots affect it.

Chapters
0:00 Crawl budget: what it is
1:08 Component 1: capacity limit
3:00 Component 2: crawl demand
4:14 Freshness: how often pages change
5:47 Two key nuances
7:12 Capacity is shared by all Google crawlers
8:29 Who should worry about it
9:44 How crawling works, simplified
11:11 Red flag: Discovered - not indexed
11:56 The practical rule
13:32 What eats the budget
14:33 Long redirect chains
16:16 What works
18:11 lastmod and freshness for AI
19:17 What doesn’t work
20:26 How to get more crawl budget
21:42 Diagnostics in four steps
22:44 New in 2026: the 2 MB fetch limit
25:47 AI bots and crawl budget
26:40 AI bots: the numbers
28:15 AI bots: what to do
28:56 Summary: priority order

What eats the budget

faceted navigation and URL parameters
internal search result pages
soft 404s, including out-of-stock pages
long redirect chains
duplicates, slow database queries, cache-busting parameters on JS and CSS

What doesn’t work

noindex: Google still fetches the page
robots.txt doesn’t move the budget to other pages
crawl-delay: Google ignores it

How to get more

a faster, more stable server (errors and slow responses lower the limit)
better pages and a better site overall

Priority order

Server speed and stability, including the database
Clean up the URL inventory
Sitemaps and internal links
Verify everything in your own logs

All 17 slides from this video as a PDF (free): https://mishamanko.gumroad.com/l/crawl-budget

Links
Crawl budget for large sites (Google): https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/large-site-managing-crawl-budget
Crawl Stats report (Search Console Help): https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/9679690
How to verify Googlebot in your logs: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/verifying-googlebot

#SEO #CrawlBudget #TechnicalSEO

metadata.title: Crawled - Currently Not Indexed: How to Fix It (Live Site, Real Data)
metadata.author: Misha Manko
metadata.shortDescription:
Crawled - currently not indexed means Google visited your page and decided not to keep it. It’s a quality decision, not an error, and clicking “Request indexing” won’t change it.

I go through it on a live site with real Search Console data: about 6,000 pages in this status, now around 100. What’s normal to see in the report, what isn’t, what every status means, what actually brings pages back, and what doesn’t.

Chapters
0:00 Crawled - currently not indexed on a live site
0:34 What the status means
1:12 Why Request Indexing won’t fix it
1:47 Quality on 3 levels: site, page, template
2:40 Pages move between statuses
3:37 Is AI content OK?
4:55 JavaScript: an empty page for Google
5:55 CDN rules that block Googlebot
6:48 How fast pages recover
7:14 What is normal to see here
8:10 What is not normal
8:38 Indexing statuses explained
11:43 What actually works
12:09 Local pages: 50 cities, one text
14:35 Near-identical products: one selector page
15:46 Copied supplier content
18:31 Content nobody reads
19:07 Crawl budget explained
20:43 Fewer pages, more rankings
21:34 What doesn’t work: indexing shortcuts
23:14 Beat the 1,000-row limit
24:49 Server and CDN logs: the source of truth
27:44 How long until you see changes
28:56 The short version
30:09 Check the HTML Google sees

What actually works

merge near-identical pages: one strong page beats 50 clones
make local and template pages really different: real photos, prices, FAQs, reviews
rewrite copied supplier text and use your own photos
remove or noindex pages nobody reads
link to the pages that matter

What doesn’t work

spamming “Request indexing”
indexing services, the Indexing API, IndexNow, sitemap pings, posting URLs on X

How long it takes

days for technical fixes
about 2 weeks is normal
4 weeks with no change: something is wrong
quality fixes on big sites can take months

All 36 slides from this video as a PDF (free): https://mishamanko.gumroad.com/l/crawled-not-indexed

Links
Page indexing report (Search Console Help): https://support.google.com/webmasters/answer/7440203
Google on AI-generated content: https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/02/google-search-and-ai-content
Crawl budget for large sites: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/large-site-managing-crawl-budget
How to verify Googlebot in your logs: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/verifying-googlebot

#SEO #GoogleSearchConsole #TechnicalSEO

Hey guys! You've probably heard about crawl budget, but do you know how it can impact your SEO? In this video, we dive deep into crawl budget, explaining when it's an issue, how it affects your rankings, and how to optimize it for better SEO performance.

Crawl budget is how much of your website Googlebot spends crawling your pages. If Google is wasting time on low-value pages, your important pages may not be crawled as often, which can lead to unstable or stagnant rankings. We’ll show you exactly how to check for crawl budget issues using Google Search Console, how to identify problematic pages, and what you can do to fix it.

If you're running an ecommerce store, publisher site, or a large blog, crawl budget matters. Let's get started and make sure Google is spending its time on the right pages!

कोशिश करें कि ना ही करें दूसरा XML साइट मैप का यूज़ करें। उसमें जो भी प्रेफर्ड पेजेस हैं जिनको आप इंडेक्स कराना चाहते हैं, क्रॉल कराना चाहते हैं, उसका यूज़ करें। डुप्लीकेट और पैरामीटर यूआरएल को बिल्कुल कंट्रोल करें। हो सके तो आप उन्हें डिसअलाउ कर दें रोबोट.txt के थ्रू। ठीक [घंटी की आवाज़] है? ऑलरेडी ये सब चीजें हम ऑलरेडी डिस्कस कर चुके हैं। होपफुली आज की क्लास आपके लिए हेल्पफुल रही हो। अगर कोई क्वेश्चन या डाउट हो तो प्लीज डू लेट मी नो इन द कमेंट सेक्शन। अदरवाइज आप ऑफलाइन क्लासेस करना चाहते हैं या लाइव ऑनलाइन क्लासेस करना चाहते हैं, इवन हम हाइब्रिड मोड देते हैं। इवन अगर आपका फोकस है जॉब के लिए, फ्रीलांसिंग के लिए, बिजनेस प्रमोट करने के लिए तो आप एनएसआईएम की क्लासेस भी ज्वाइन कर सकते हैं। कोर्स ज्वाइन करने के लिए नीचे नंबर भी मेंशन है और वेबसाइट की लिंक भी मेंशन है। आप डायरेक्टली हमारे डिजिटल मार्केटिंग एक्सपर्ट से कांटेक्ट कर कर हमारी कोर्सेस की डिटेल्स भी ले सकते हैं। थैंक यू ऑल।

metadata.title: Crawl Budget: SEO Mythbusting
metadata.author: Google Search Central
metadata.shortDescription:
In the second episode of SEO Mythbusting season 2, Martin Splitt (Developer Advocate, Google) and Alexis Sanders (Senior Account Manager, Merkle) discuss the most common SEO questions and myths around crawl budget.

Specific timestamped topics discussed in this episode:
Why is crawl budget an interesting topic to discuss (0:00)
What is crawl budget? (1:15)
What is crawl rate, and what is crawl demand? (1:47)
How does Googlebot make its crawl rate and crawl demand decisions? (2:44)
ETags, HTTP headers, last modified dates, and similar (3:43)
What size of sites should worry about crawl budget? (4:35)
Server setup vs crawl budget (5:00)
Crawl frequency vs quality of content (6:18)
What to expect to see in one’s log files if Google is testing one’s server? (7:45)
Tips on how to get your site crawled accurately during a site migration (8:18)
Crawl budget and the different levels of one’s site’s infrastructure (9:40)
Does crawl budget affect rendering as well? (10:37)
Caching of resources and crawl budget (11:46)
Crawl budget and specific industries such as publishing (13:34)
What can be - generally speaking - recommended to help Googlebot out when crawling one’s site? (15:03)
What are the usual pitfalls people get into with crawl budget? (16:52)
Can one tell Googlebot to crawl one’s site more? (17:40)

Documentation mentioned in this episode:
What Crawl Budget means for Googlebot → https://goo.gle/3iIJHp2
How to move your content to a new location → https://goo.gle/3iKf2HS 
Reduce the Googlebot crawl rate → https://goo.gle/38LfMb5

Watch more SEO Mythbusting episodes → 
https://goo.gle/SEO-Mythbusting  
Subscribe to Google Search Central → https://goo.gle/SearchCentral

#SEO #GoogleSearch
